## 2026-10-24 session round 7: asm-block frame split reaches EXACT on the blitter

`0x47a320` is now EXACT 586/586 with zero relocations as a normal C function
`void __cdecl fcn_0047a320(int, int, int, int)` whose `__asm` block covers only
0x47a326..0x47a564. Two measured facts made it byte-exact:

- The compiler owns the outer frame when the C wrapper declares four arguments:
  c2 emits `push ebp; mov ebp,esp; push ebx/esi/edi` and the matching
  `pop edi/esi/ebx/ebp; ret`. Declaring the wrapper with fewer arguments drops
  the frame and the object comes out 582 bytes instead of 586.
- MASM will not encode the 23 absolute scratch/mask operands inline: an absolute
  memory operand is rejected, `ds:[...]` adds a 0x3e prefix, and extern C
  symbols introduce abs32 relocations (RELOC 586/586 but not EXACT). Those
  instructions are emitted as their exact native bytes through per-byte `_emit`,
  each annotated with the native mnemonic.

`source document-assembly` receipts are recorded for both hand-written rows
(`fcn_0047a320` source hash 11cba0f9..., `fcn_0041bb70` source hash e4698bda...);
no `__declspec(naked)` is used, so lint E023 stays satisfied. The same split
(frame in C, hand-written body in `__asm`, `_emit` for absolute operands) is now
the documented route for the remaining assembly rows. Decision: lead.

## 2026-10-24 session round 7: first EXACT hand-written-asm row through inline asm

`0x41bb70` is reconstructed as a normal `void __cdecl fcn_0041bb70(int pixel,
char *out1, char *out2, char *out3)` whose body is one `__asm { }` block, and
`rebrew test` records EXACT 317/317 with zero relocations. No `__declspec(naked)`
is used, so lint E023 stays satisfied. Measured code end is 0x41bcac (317
bytes); the stored 320 included three alignment NOPs and the metadata size
follows the measured extent.

Two MSVC 6 inline-assembly facts from this row, worth reusing for the other
hand-written blocks: `pushaw`/`popaw` are not mnemonics there (C2400), so the
PUSHA/POPA opcode is `_emit 0x66` followed by `_emit 0x60`/`_emit 0x61`; and
naming ebx/esi/edi inside the block makes MSVC emit its own entry push/pop
prologue, which shifts every byte, so those saves and the absolute
`mov eax,[0x14ce86c]` load go through `_emit` bytes too. The compiler's own
trailing return supplies the final ret. Receipt: agent report in session; source
`src/GOLDTL.fcn_0041bb70.c`. Decision: lead.

## 2026-10-24 session round 7: inline assembly is the route for hand-written asm rows

The remaining GoldTL STUB set includes rows that are not compiler output:
`0x41bb70` contains `0x60` PUSHAD/PUSHAW at two sites with full register
save/restore around 16-bit mask operations, and `0x47a320` is a manual-register
sprite/mask blitter with a shared epilogue and four copy/merge loops. Both are
hand-written assembly in the original source.

Lint E023 forbids a whole-function `__declspec(naked)` body, but inline
`__asm { ... }` inside an ordinary C function is already used by this project
(`src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/spiel.c`,
`src/Develop/Units/m_alloc/m_alloc.c`). The reviewed route is therefore a normal
C function whose body reproduces the native instructions in inline asm, with
`rebrew source document-assembly` recording the positive evidence (PUSHAD is not
compiler-emitted; manual register banking). Tasks 92 and 94 carry that
instruction; assignment and STATUS stay in the normal per-row flow. Decision:
lead, following docs/assembly-audit.md.

## 2026-10-24 session round 6: upstream batch binding writer and `library adopt`

Two upstream additions in `/home/maci/Desktop/Projects/relumea/repos/rebrew`:

- `rebrew.metadata.binding_history.change_source_bindings_batch` applies a
  reviewed list of retire/rebind changes in one metadata write. Each change gets
  its own binding history, a conflict rejects the whole batch before
  publication, and the preview digest guards apply. The single-row function now
  shares the same validation and document-mutation helpers; behavior is
  unchanged. Tests: `tests/test_source_binding.py::TestBatchBindingChanges`.
- `rebrew library adopt` records a unique stock-archive match over a FUNCTION or
  STUB row: it re-runs the project's archive match, requires one unique
  candidate, refuses vendored objects, writes the LIBRARY identity under the
  archive family's header, and guards the write with a preview digest.
  Supporting refactor: `lib_match.project_match_index` isolates the index
  construction the CLI and adopt share. Tests: `tests/test_library_adopt.py`,
  docs: `docs/CLI.md`. `identify_library.prepare_library_header` is now public
  so the two writers share it.

`change_source_binding`: kind LIBRARY, file `references/zlib/<unit>.c`, the
native symbol, the reviewed reason, and the previewed metadata digest. This is
the same row shape `library bind-source` writes for a vendored library.

`.scratch/lead/adopt_zlib_rows.py` performs the batch. It re-checks that the
source file contains the matched C function name, previews each rebind,
retries only the concurrent-metadata race, and backs the replaced bodies up
under `.scratch/lead/adopted-bodies/` before deleting them. All 21 rows now
carry kind LIBRARY and no byte status; `rebrew lint --json` is clean (7263
files, zero errors, zero warnings). The 173 remaining stock-libc matches
cannot use this path because their provider is a toolchain archive member with
no project source file; they need the reviewed `library adopt` command
proposed in the upstream IDEAS-GUILD. Commands and receipts:
`.scratch/lead/adopt_zlib_rows.py`, `.scratch/lead/library-stubs.json`.

## 2026-10-23 session round 4: client inventory padding repair

Found 775 Gold and 10 GoldTL STUB rows whose stored extent ran past the last
reachable instruction into linker fill. The survey walks control flow from the
entry (following in-row jumps, stopping at ret or an out-of-row jump), takes the
latest flow-exiting instruction, and requires every byte to the next inventory
start to be 0x90, 0xCC or 0x00; a first version that used linear disassembly
alone was discarded because unreachable data can mimic fill. 690 Gold and 10
GoldTL rows qualified (`.scratch/lead/survey_padding2.py`).

Applied the repairs in digest-guarded chunks of 100 through
`binary repair-extents` (`.scratch/lead/repair_padding.py`), then aligned stored
SIZE in one `set_fields_batch` write with the `fix-sizes` tag
(`.scratch/lead/sync_padding_sizes.py`). The per-row `update_field` loop that
ran first rewrites the 30 MB store for every row and would have taken over an
hour; the batch writer finished 547 rows in one write. Re-running the survey
reports zero remaining fill tails on both clients, inventory sizes equal stored
SIZE for all 700 rows, and `rebrew lint --json` is clean (7284 files, zero
errors, zero warnings). The old extent survives in each row's `extent_history`,
so a wrong repair is reversible with another reviewed size change. Decision:
Lead.

## 2026-10-25 session round 36: provider presence test, byte-identity blocker

Method: parse each candidate archive's COFF members, mask every relocation operand
in each function-level `.text` COMDAT, and search the reference `.text` for the
resulting wildcard pattern. A provider whose objects the reference linked must
produce exact masked matches for essentially all of its sections.

Scores: DirectX 8.1 SDK (Oct 2001, sha256 39a8e218..., now vendored) 28.0%;
DirectX 8.0 SDK 25.1%; DirectX 9.0 SDK (Dec 2002 and Mar 2004, identical archive
sha256 0d5bd10b...) 27.9%; XP SP1 Intel archive (previous vendor) 28.5%. Spot
check at the known band owner `0x5e6d72` finds no match from the vendored archive
near that VA, so the band bytes were never reproduced by the vendored archive.

Conclusion: the reference's static D3DX8 code came from a build not present in
this environment (different compiler build or flags), and no source tree on disk
carries the D3DX8 implementation (only headers and VB bindings). The band is
roughly 450 KB of `.text`; whole-file byte identity cannot be reached without
those exact object bytes or the sources and original flags. Recorded as the
blocking condition. Evidence: `.scratch/lead/member-presence.json`,
`.scratch/lead/compare_providers.py`, `.scratch/dx8sdk/`, `references/dxsdk8/VENDOR.md`.
Decision: Lead. Final tree state: headers match, imports 5 missing/2 added,
`.text` 2,444,492, `.rdata` 47,460, `.data` 15,715,076, EXACT 300, RELOC 3,535,
SIZE_MISMATCH 1,023, NEAR_MATCHING 83, PROVEN 5, lint 0 errors.

## 2026-10-25 session round 56: upstream lint E023 honors documented assembly

Upstream bug: `rebrew lint` E023 rejected whole-function `__declspec(naked)` bodies
even when the definition carried current `source document-assembly` evidence, while
W020 already exempts documented assembly. That made the project's evidenced-assembly
rule unusable for C++ member rows the C frontend cannot express (`__thiscall`).

Fix in the upstream checkout (`src/rebrew/lint.py`): extracted
`_documented_assembly_symbols()` (the hash-checked provenance lookup W020 used),
passed it into `_check_E023_naked_asm()`, and the check now exempts a naked definition
whose own symbol has current documented evidence. Stale evidence does not exempt.
Regression tests added to `tests/test_lint.py` (`TestE023DocumentedAssembly`, three
cases: documented exempt, undocumented still flagged, stale evidence flagged);
`tests/test_lint.py` passes 264 tests.

Project verification after reinstalling the checkout editable: `rebrew lint --json`
reports 0 errors and 149 warnings. The two converted member rows (0x60e654 EXACT
88/88, 0x60cde0 EXACT 89/89) are the reason whole-function naked assembly exists here.
Decision: Lead.

Also recorded for the slice workflow: `rebrew test` persists a verdict by default, so
a rejected experimental body can demote an accepted NEAR/EXACT row. The slice spec now
requires `--no-promote` for trials and a second run without it to persist accepted
results.

Measured the three sections that decide file bytes:

  5,102 bytes larger and every following section shifts.
- .rdata: reference 76,722 bytes at 0x662000, build 47,702 bytes at 0x663000 (29,020
  missing, and the base moves 4,096 bytes later).
- .data: reference 15,766,564 virtual / 266,240 raw at 0x675000, build 4,596,708
  virtual / 143,360 raw at 0x66f000 (raw data 122,880 bytes short and the base shifts
  again).
- Raw .text agreement is 68,386 bytes (2.74%); the first differing byte is at 0x401025
  and is an absolute data operand (0x6624a0 vs 0x7ff018), so early text differences are
  data displacement rather than body errors.

Content is present but unordered: of 1,082 reference .rdata printable strings, 821
(76%) also appear in the build, but the ordered sequences agree for only 3 leading
entries; .data has 4,759 reference strings, 2,446 present (51%), ordered agreement 26.
Our translation-unit layout therefore pools literals in a different order from the
reference.

Consequence: byte identity needs three things at once, function bodies whose compiled
sizes equal native extents (.text is currently +5,102), every referenced data object
defined (.rdata -29,020, .data raw -122,880), and source/literal ordering equal to the
reference so section bases land at 0x662000 and 0x675000. A data reconstruction pass
that emits reference-ordered byte regions in one translation unit is the only way to
close the latter two, and it does not exist yet in the project.

Tooling note: `rebrew test --size N` behaves as a floor, not an exact window. It
compares max(N, obj_size) bytes, so --size 177 against a 181-byte object reports
total 181 and --size 165 against a 177-byte object reports total 177; padding
beyond ret always counts as mismatch unless the object happens to fill the window.
Worth an upstream issue.

## 2026-10-26 session round 86: 0x4f5cc0 compacted-switch threshold measured

0x4f5cc0 (64 B) is a hard encoding wall under the project's `/O2 /Gd` frameless
config, confirmed by exhaustive shape/flag sweeps in `.scratch/f5cc/`. The reference
dispatch is the two-level compacted table (`dec ecx; cmp ecx,6; ja`;
`xor edx; mov dl,[ecx+0x4f5cf8]`; `jmp [edx*4+0x4f5cf0]`) with a 7-entry byte map and
a 2-entry dword table. MSVC's compaction is gated on the switch RANGE, not on case
count, target sharing, or selector type: under `/O2`, a range-7 selector emits a
direct `jmp [reg*4]` table for every spelling tried (dense contiguous N=7..24; sparse
1/3/5/7; char and int selectors; num_unique 1 and 2), while the compacted form first
appears at range ~25 (char A/C/F/Z) and range 30 (int 10/20/30/40). The flags that
force compaction on a range-7 switch (`/Ot /Oy /Ob2 /Op /Oa` alone) also turn on the
frame pointer, breaking the reference's frameless `mov ecx,[esp+8]` prologue, and no
`/O2`+extra combination yields compaction. Because the direct table is 28 B against
the reference's 16 B of tables, the object is always 68 B vs the 64 B row (SIZE_MISMATCH),
so the size cannot be reached without the compacted dispatch. File left at its best
state, the per-case-return variant, 40/68 (was 40/68; no change). Decision: lead task,
no source or metadata edit. Evidence: `uv run rebrew test src/GOLDTL.fcn_004f5cc0.c
--va 0x4f5cc0 --size 64 --no-promote` = SIZE_MISMATCH 40/68 obj 68.

Exact final measurement (`flock .scratch/lead/test-0.lock uv run rebrew test
src/fcn_00515340.c --va 0x515340 --size 165 --no-promote --json`):


## 2026-10-26 GOLDTL 0x467870: STUB 136 -> RELOC 176/176

The row was rebuilt to 136/176 (object 170) with two residual defects: the missing
third `g_1015ea0` reload in the tail (6 bytes) and every two-register table access
emitted with the base/index roles swapped (`[edi+esi+disp]` against the reference
`[esi+edi+disp]`). The pointer-arithmetic form `*(int*)(rec + tbl + disp)` cannot
flip those roles under msvc-6.0-sp5-pp /O2: char*/int typing, operand order,
int+int casts, and inline-vs-variable strides all measure the same SIB choice.

The working spelling is the struct-index idiom on the named global, matching the
`((Def*)g_772500)[idx]` form in fcn_004659c0: a local 0x2f4-stride
`fcn_00467870_Def` (fields at 0x0c/0x10/0x14/0x8c/0x90/0x94/0x9c) and
`((fcn_00467870_Def*) g_1015ea0)[idx].field` per access. The named extern lvalue
lets /O2 keep the loaded table pointer register-resident within a phase, reload
it after each of the three call groups (`fcn_0047b620` and `__ftol`), and place
the offset in the SIB base slot, reproducing all three reference loads
(`mov eax/edi/edx, [0x1015ea0]`) and every `[esi+reg+disp]` access. The raw
`*(char**)0x1015ea0` spelling does not get that treatment and fails.

## 2026-10-26 GOLDTL 0x4127a0: STUB 55 -> NEAR_MATCHING 95/130

The row was a STUB at 55/130: the if-branch loaded a/b/c into a rotated
register set (EDX/EAX/ECX against the reference EAX/ECX/EDX) and the else-branch
store of `d` came after both `a` and `b` stores instead of interleaving.

The winning shape keeps three locals in the save branch (load a, b, c; store a;
store b; direct `*(int*)0x6b5c70 = *(int*)0x6b5c84`; constants; late c store)
and adds a fourth local `d` in the restore branch only, with restore loads in
source order c, a, b and the statements

```
*(int*) 0x6772bc = a;
d = *(int*) 0x6b5c70;
*(int*) 0x6772c0 = b;
*(int*) 0x6b5c84 = d;
*(int*) 0x6b5c80 = c;
```

The interleaved `d` assignment is what makes MSVC emit the reference schedule
(store a; load d into the freed register; store b; store d; store c). Six
else-load permutations of the same body measured 85-95; c,a,b (and the
equivalent a,c,b / c,b,a) all reach 95. Remaining 35 mismatched bytes are the
save-branch load rotation (offsets 8-37, 67) plus the restore-branch load
rotation (84, 89-96, 101, 107, 113, 119); declaration order, `register` hints,
unsigned loads, chained constant stores, struct/pair loads, early-return
polarity, and direct (local-free) memory copies all measure the same or worse.

Verification: `flock .scratch/lead/test-2.lock uv run rebrew test
src/fcn_004127a0.c --va 0x4127a0 --size 130 --no-promote --json` = NEAR_MATCHING
95/130, obj 130, reloc 0. Not promoted (no EXACT/RELOC).

Conflict resolution split across two workers. ~198 rows cleared via locked `rebrew data set`
(majority .c declaration as canonical, plus 6 typed from reference-binary bytes and 27 from
source usage), and the final ~33 (plus a residue) via FIX-1 header demotion: 57 minority-type
`extern` lines moved byte-exactly out of 54 `.c` files into 54 new single-includer
`*_gconf.h` headers, so the competing type becomes header-only and drops out of the
comparison. No type value changed in any file, so no codegen moved. Two alias/view rows were
also needed: g_7e3a44/48, g_7e3a54/58, g_772580 marked `--storage-kind alias --backing`
(their canonical `float[3]`/array owners span them), clearing W038 row overlaps.

A server.dll regression surfaced during this round and was fixed. GOLDTL byte-match work on
shared source had wrapped alchemistry's ahm_ExAllocAlchemist logs in `#if defined(REBREW_GOLD)`,
but no target ever defines `REBREW_GOLD`, so the guard was dead in all builds. GOLD's and
TL's references genuinely lack those logs, but server.dll's reference HAS them (string present
in original/Server/server.dll, absent in both client references). The dead guard therefore
stripped ~32 bytes of log+goto code from server.dll, shifting the .text section by 0x20 and
cascading into 118,470 differing bytes (58.68% match). Fixed by re-keying the three alchemistry
guards to `#if defined(REBREW_TARGET_SERVER)` (the only target that compiles this code), since
server is the only reference with the logs. server.dll is byte-identical again: 286,720/286,720,
SHA-256 3cc2ce9049e41ab6 = original/Server/server.dll.

This is the general lesson for shared-source byte matching: a body edit tuned to one target's
reference can silently break another target that shares the file. Where a target's reference
genuinely differs, the divergence must be guarded by a macro the differing target actually
defines (server defines REBREW_TARGET_SERVER; no target defines REBREW_GOLD).

Final state: RELOC 3,698 EXACT 437, STUB 59, NEAR 34, SIZE_MISMATCH 1,015, matched annotation
bytes 818,598. NO_FUNCTION 0, NO_SOURCE 0, covered 5208/5208. TL rebuilt: imports/headers/
layout match, same-offset 104,786 of 2,850,888 (3.68%). server.dll byte-identical. Lint
0 errors/0 warnings, data conflicts 0. Decision: Lead.

  it now skips anchors whose claim moved.

  shared helper and pulled that target's closures into the link.

  row: 412 of 430 are mapped, 93 early and 244 late, but every early one is off
  by 1-9 MB, and no early displacement is under 0x4000, so an intra-TU pad
  cannot express them. The moderate errors are all late, which padding cannot
  undo.
- **Moving all 304 `_dpad_` declarations into one tail TU** (pads linked last
  instead of displacing their owner's successors). Deduplicated 304 pads to 303
  addresses; the match fell 249,858 -> 231,287, reverted from the per-file
  backups.
- **Shrinking text lead pads where the boundary had become late.** 87 shrinks
  left three TUs uncompilable (the replacement did not keep the declaration
  well formed) and produced no byte gain; pads were stripped and regenerated.

The regeneration cycle reproduces the exact 249,858 score from the same tree,
which confirms the pads are deterministic function of the current map. Both
passes are now fixed points: data converge reports no adjustments, `fill` zero
pads, text caps above 0x2000 revert, and removing pads drops the match.

Verified: TL links, lint 0 errors / 0 warnings, data conflicts 0, STATUS
unchanged (RELOC 3,685 / EXACT 415 / SIZE_MISMATCH 1,046 / NEAR 36 / STUB 2),
same-offset 249,858 (8.76%). Decision: Lead. Next match requires recovering the
short bodies at the leading drift points, not more padding.

## 2026-10-29: converge regression and a coherent rebuild (8.78% -> 8.32%)

`data layout converge` was run on the 250,282 state to test one more adjustment
(it wanted a 2,612-byte pad move). The applied pad changed the .data ensemble and
the same-offset match fell to 176,858. Restoring the pad from the reference with
the converge formula never reproduced the lost bytes: neither the recorded size,
the pre-converge size, zeros, nor a file-offset shift brought the data matches
back. The 72 KB of lost matches were those pads' reference-byte fill, and the
exact ensemble that produced them cannot be rebuilt from the current sources.

Recovery used the deterministic pipeline the tools already provide:

1. strip every `_dpad_`, `_dlead_` and `_tlead_` declaration (396 blocks);
2. rebuild (104,220 bare);
3. `data layout fill` (52 init, 127 BSS pads) -> rebuild (146,365);
4. `data layout converge` -> rebuild (155,195);
5. text lead pass at caps 0x800 and 0x2000 -> 237,148.

A second converge cycle and caps 0x4000-0x20000 were measured and reverted. The
tree is coherent and reproducible now, but the state is 13,134 bytes below the
previous best (250,282) because the old pad ensemble is gone. The old image is
kept at `.scratch/organize/best-250282.exe`; sources no longer reproduce it.

Lesson recorded for the next rounds: converge must not be applied without a
byte-match guard between saves, which is exactly the gap in upstream
`docs/IDEAS-GUILD.md` (commit `6fed48d2`).

Verified: TL links, lint 0 errors / 0 warnings after rebinding seven stale type
records, data conflicts 0, same-offset 237,148 (8.32%). Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-29: EXTRACT_ERROR accounting bug fixed upstream

Verify reported EXTRACT_ERROR for eight rows whose bodies matched: the stored
COFF symbol carried a decoration the compiled definition did not (`@20` stdcall
spelling against a cdecl/naked body; then cdecl `_f_foo` against a `__fastcall`

body bytes were comparable, and `status` then subtracted those rows.

- `2414e470`: when no spelling variant matches, take the object symbol whose

layering check passes (the first attempt imported `gen_stubs` from
`compiler/`, which the import-direction rule rejects, so the demangler is a
local helper). Project effect after reinstalling from `main`: all eight rows
verify, EXTRACT_ERROR leaves STATUS, EXACT rises 463 -> 471, matched bytes
1,279,961 -> 1,280,303.

Branch note: the checkout was on `release/6.7.0` (not `main`), so the fixes went
to `main` by cherry-pick and the checkout was returned to `release/6.7.0`
untouched.

## 2026-10-30: placed mismatch rows are score-positive when a pad can compensate

Found 47 SIZE_MISMATCH rows whose linked VA already equals the reference VA
(42,001 bytes total). Changing one of those bodies raises the same-offset score
directly, provided the size delta is absorbed by the text pad of the immediately
following object, which keeps every later offset unchanged.

First case `0x004102a0` (110 bytes): the reference passes the three values as
`int*` and converts through `fild dword ptr [reg]`, not by value. With
`void** a1, int* v1, int* v2, int* v3` and the stores ordered 0x9c, 0xa0, 0x98
the body goes 54 -> 73 matched bytes and 102 -> 108 bytes. Shrinking
`_tlead_GOLDTL_fcn_00412b10` from 80 to 74 bytes absorbed the 6-byte growth; the
linked image moves 237,149 -> 237,168 with no downstream shift.

The rule matters: the pad must belong to the object that immediately follows the
edited one. `0x004b6a00` needs one trailing reference `nop` byte, but its next
pad owner is far downstream (`fcn_005b6300`), so the one-byte insert shifted
intermediate bodies and cost 3,158 bytes; that change was reverted.

Verified: row 0x004102a0 at 73/110, image 237,168 (8.32%), lint 0 errors /
0 warnings, data conflicts 0. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-11-01: data-prefix padding aligns .data content; new best 259,891

The `.data` section starts where `.text`+`.rdata` end, so its content sits
0x2C000 before the reference's `.data` and the file-offset comparison of data
bytes ran at the wrong internal shift. End-of-text padding cannot fix that: a
simulation over 0x0000-0x22000 of tail padding showed the unpadded image is
always best (any pad replaces the tail content that already matches). Prefix
padding inside `.data` moves only that section's content, and a simulation over
0x0-0x30000 predicted 259,311 at 0x2B000.

Measured on real builds: 0x2B000 -> 259,369 (the simulation was within 58 bytes),
then swept 0x1000, 0x400, 0x100, 0x10 steps to the optimum 0x2B530 -> 259,891.
One caveat learned the hard way: `= {0}` compiles to BSS, so the array grows the
virtual size and the raw size stays unchanged; one non-zero initializer puts the
array in `.data` and yields the raw zeros the alignment needs.

Same-offset score 244,344 -> 259,891 (+15,547), file 2,854,912 -> 3,031,040
bytes. `verify --whole-binary` reports imports, layout and headers matching; lint
0 errors / 0 warnings, data conflicts 0. STATUS after re-earning linked EXACT:
EXACT 466 / RELOC 3,632 / NEAR 34 / SIZE_MISMATCH 1,050.

Documented in docs/msvc6-link-layout.md section 93. The pad is not managed by
`data layout fill`; future pad regeneration must preserve it.

Decision: Lead.

## 2026-11-01: .rdata prefix pad pairs with the .data pad; 260,232

`.rdata` content also starts early (0x23F000 versus 0x262000). A prefix pad
inside `.rdata` moves only that section, and taking the same byte count out of the
`.data` prefix keeps the data content at its measured offset. Emitted with

deltas: 29 of 64 scanned members keep one constant delta across all located

reference and only placement is wrong. Examples: LIBCMT sbheap −0x229F2, util

(the gap bytes replace currently matching content).

The way forward is explicit member ordering: link extracted members as a response
file in reference-start order, with a generated gap pad between neighbours. That
needs per-member start estimates (median of located VA minus symbol offset), a
complete member set including the members whose bodies are not locatable, and the
archive scan disabled so no duplicate extraction occurs. Not attempted this
round; image stays 260,232, lint 0 errors / 0 warnings.

## 2026-11-03: SaveBMP24 loop reconstruction stalls at 17 structural diffs

Second-closest placed body: `SaveBMP24` (448 bytes, 140 exact / 10 reloc / 20
structural). The target's pixel loop is decodable: p = src+1, dst = row+2,
counting down, reading p[0], p[-1], p[-2] and writing dst[-2], dst[-1], dst[0],
with p += 3 and dst += 3. Encoding that exactly breaks the function's register
allocation elsewhere (exact drops to 45, invalid 1), because the pointer bases
force a different allocation for the header writes.

Intermediate forms: `p += 3` before the reads with p[-1..-3] gives 439 bytes, 143
exact / 17 structural (best); reverse store order and swap-decl are worse
(21 and 97 structural); dst-base forms worse (84). Target also carries nine
trailing nop bytes (448 vs 439). Source restored; image unchanged at raw
271,837, informative 92,169 (3.87%), lint 0 errors / 0 warnings, conflicts 0.
Decision: Lead.

## 2026-11-03: the library band holds application code, not just libraries

Of the 1,490 inventory functions at VAs 0x5E0060-0x660ACE, 937 match extracted

band is a mixture. A single-order link cannot reproduce that: objects,
then archives, with no second object phase. Next step is a two-phase link model
(some objects after the archive scan), which needs object files compiled outside
the main target's source list.

miss. This closes the alignment line: further layout work would need reordering

a single-order link cannot express.

## 2026-11-03: fcn_0040ED40 tail decoded to an options-copy dance

The 17 structural diffs sit in the `D3_ANIMATION_OPTIONS` block before the
`fcn_00434970` call. The target builds the by-value argument from a stack copy:
it keeps the original byte in `al`, sets and clears individual flag bits
(`or dl,2`, `and al,0xfd`, `or al,1`), stores the copy at `[esp+0x14]`/`[esp+0x1c]`,
then materialises the 12-byte argument on the stack before `push`ing it. The
candidate reaches the same call with the fields written in source order and
without the extra register copy dance, hence the different instruction order.

The source currently writes `*(int*) &options = 0;` after `memset` and sets
`mode`, then `layer`, `queue`, `mode` again, `loop`, `reverse`. The target's bit
twiddling suggests it modified the struct through bitfields after a copy, which
is a source-shape question for the next round. Lint 0 errors / 0 warnings, data
conflicts 0. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-30: multi-function character TU drives the 0x402b00 placement drift; splitting one body did not fix order

(delta 0 through 0x402aa0), then `ch_UpdatePendingPositions` lands at 0x402B00

275,568 -> 275,542 / 93,703 -> 93,670. Reverted the split, the rebind and the
build: score back to 275,568 / 93,703, tree clean.

build's anchor ordering, not from splitting sources alone. Lint 0 errors /
0 warnings. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-30: upstream source split learns --occurrence for duplicate definitions

Implemented the gap filed in round 235 against the upstream checkout: `rebrew
source split --va VA --occurrence N` selects the Nth C definition (source order)
when a VA has several, which is what mutually exclusive preprocessor branches
produce. It requires `--va`, out-of-range values name the definition count in the
error, and definitions inside a preprocessor conditional stay refused because
extracting one leaves the conditional unbalanced.

Tests: new case in tests/test_split.py covers the refusal without the flag, the
range error, selection of the second definition and the requires-`--va` guard;

flag, so `command.c`/`friedhof_logic.c` still cannot split there, and their
definitions sit inside `#if`/`#else` anyway, which the extraction still refuses.

expression's operand order, so C spelling does not move it. Restored the original
body. No score change: 292,292 / 108,702. Lint 0 errors / 0 warnings, data

## 2026-10-30: ch_AttachAni frame model from the exact prologue

Using the instruction addresses in `original/Europa1400Gold_TL.exe` (the earlier
diff listed only indices), the cdecl argument pushes stay on the stack until
`add esp,0x2c` at 0x404e17, which changes every later offset:

- entry esp E: arg1 obj at E+4, arg2 name at E+8.
- `sub esp,0x430`; `push ebx`; `push ebp`; then `mov ebp,[esp+0x440]` reads E+8,
  so ebp = name.
- after `push esi`; `push edi`; `push ebp`; `call 0x42E540`, the return leaves the
  pushed argument on the stack, so `mov edi,[esp+0x448]` reads E+4, obj.
- the two sprintf calls then use obj+0x130, name and obj+0x130 for
  "character/%s/%s_%s.baf", and obj+0x130, name for "%s_%s".
- `add esp,0x2c` restores esp to E-0x43C, and `mov al,[esp+0x450]` then reads
  E+0x14, which is a fifth argument position under a three-argument model.

That last read is the open question: either the function takes more arguments than
the current `ch_AttachAni(int, char*, unsigned char)` prototype, or some of the
0x2c bytes belong to other cleanups. The next step is to test the two candidate
prototypes against the compiler and grep the callers for their push counts.

State unchanged: raw 292,336 / informative 108,675, lint 0 errors / 0 warnings,
data conflicts 0. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-30: the .rdata shortfall is library-owned GUID and float tables

Our `.rdata` is 53,248 raw bytes against the reference 77,824, a 24,576-byte
shortfall that also shifts the `.data` base by +0x6000. Scanning the reference
`.rdata` in 16-byte windows found 2,674 windows with no match anywhere in our
`.rdata`, grouped into 216 runs. Largest: RVA 0xB190 (10,880 B), 0x9A50
(5,504 B), 0xDC20 (4,576 B), 0x3400 (1,696 B), 0x11240 (1,568 B).

Contents identify the owners. RVA 0x3400 (VA 0x665400) is a float table starting
652.8 then repeating 2.0, 3.0 pairs. RVAs 0xB190/0x9A50/0xDC20 decode as DirectX
interface GUIDs (`\x00q\x95+\x9a\x9e\xcf\x11...`, IID-shaped data), so the
missing bytes belong to linked DirectX library data, not game source. The fix is to
link the archive members that carry those tables rather than to author data rows
with copied bytes.

Baseline: raw 292,336 / informative 108,675, lint 0 errors / 0 warnings, data
conflicts 0. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-30: section VAs are locked to the .text raw size, so .data operand alignment needs text to shrink

Grew the `.rdata` prefix pad from 0x1000 to 0x7000 so `.rdata` raw becomes 0x13000,
exactly the reference's `.rdata` raw size. Build clean, but `.data` moved to
0x281000, not the reference 0x275000: every section after `.text` starts at
`.text` end, and our `.text` raw is 0x26D000 against the reference 0x261000, a
+0xC000 offset. Growing `.rdata` cannot fix `.data` placement while `.text` is
49,152 bytes larger. Raw fell 292,336 -> 285,839 / 107,327, so the change also lost
`.rdata` matches; reverted.

Consequence: the `.data` operand mismatches that block many RELOC funcs come from a
section base shifted by the text excess. Fixing them requires the reconstructed
.text to shrink to the reference size, which means removing or replacing code the
reference does not carry, not padding later sections.

## 2026-10-30: the drifted strings are literal content labels, not globals

Checked the row shape before converting anything: `GOLDTL.0x0067EAE4`
(`str_bau_arbeiter_unterk`) has `storage_kind = "literal"` and a note that it is a
"compiler literal content label, not a source identifier or separate C global".
The same holds for the other six string drifts.

So defining a global array would assign the wrong storage owner. The drift is a
difference in where the compiler pools the literal, which follows translation-unit
literal order, not source values. Correcting it means reproducing the original TU's
literal order, outside the scope of a small edit. Left the call sites as inline
literals.

## 2026-10-30: ch_AttachAni frame accounting is ambiguous under the push-accurate model

Worked through the 129-instruction target with `push` accounting including the
arguments left on the stack between calls. The offsets are not self-consistent with
a three-argument cdecl frame: after `add esp,0x2c` the frame sits at E-0x46C, so
`[esp+0x450]` reads a local at E-0x20, while later `[esp+0x450]` positions (used as
an object pointer for `[obj+0x34]` and `[obj+0x88]`) read the fourth argument slot
in some readings and a local in others. The two candidate structures (four
arguments versus an extra local slot) predict different use of the same offsets.

Because an exact 404-byte reproduction depends on this layout, and the existing
body is old GA output with 120 of 129 instructions structural, the rewrite needs a
correct frame model first. Stopped short of writing a body on a guess.

## 2026-10-30: section table numbers and why a vsize-only fix is not worth it

Current built sections: `.text` va 0x1000 vsize 0x26C4C2 raw 0x26D000 (raw end
0x26E000); `.rdata` va 0x26E000 vsize 0xCD66 raw 0xD000; `.data` va 0x27B000 vsize
0x2C80BA4 raw 0xA4000 (raw end 0x31F000); `.data1` and `.rsrc` unchanged shapes.
Every symbol at or above 0x31F000 in `.data` is BSS-only.

The `.data` virtual size is 30.9 MB larger than the reference (0xF09424), from
uninitialised `_dpad_*` blobs beyond the raw region. Shrinking them to match the
header would change only the two 4-byte VirtualSize fields in the section table
(a handful of raw bytes) while moving every BSS symbol address after the first
removed blob, which is the same layout that data operands and pads depend on. The
exchange is not worth taking in the last rounds; recorded here rather than risked.

Byte score: raw 292,528 / 2,850,888, informative 108,803. Lint 0 errors / 0
warnings, data conflicts 0. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

## 2026-10-30: per-file delta attribution fails when a file's leading function is unbound

The +0xD90 drift that makes 0x4258D0 line 2,752 bytes late looked attributable to
`src/Develop/Units/Error/Error.c`: its bound row `_GetDebugRecordByIndex` sits at
+0x9B0 while the previous file is at 0. The map shows why that is an artefact:
Error.c's first linked symbols (`_CrashDumpUnhandledExceptionFilter@4` at 0x41D4D0,
then `_EmitCrashModuleLine`, `_GetDebugRecordByIndex` at 0x41DD00) already sit at
their reference VAs; the metadata row at 0x41D858 has no matching leading symbol, so
pairing the smallest metadata VA with the smallest linked symbol compares two
different functions.

Whenever a file starts with unbound functions, the per-file delta method reports a
false jump. The real drift in that window therefore is not localised by this method,
and no body fix can be justified from it.

Byte score: raw 292,528 / 2,850,888, informative 108,803. Lint 0 errors / 0
warnings, data conflicts 0. No GA was run. Decision: Lead.

Writing that store on both arms of the flag test scored NEAR 173/188 against 174/188. The single store was restored and `rebrew test` recorded NEAR 174/188. Decision: continuing TL reconstruction. The flag load still follows the value store.

## 2026-11-01 — TL 0x413d10 drops the redundant acc self-read

`fcn_00413d10` (TL `0x413d10`, placed at its reference VA) carried
`acc = *(volatile float*) &acc;` twice. The first, on the successful-call path,
bought nothing: `acc` is zero there and the write-back only pinned a stack slot.
Removing that one line and leaving the failure-path read in place raises the
comparison from 216/229 to NEAR 222/229 (exact instructions 66 to 72, structural
13 to 7), candidate still 229 bytes. The remaining seven differences are the
`k`/`width` stack-home swap (`[esp+0x10]` versus `[esp+0x14]`) and the two
`add ecx, edx` / `add ecx, eax` order; neither changed with declaration or
initialisation order. Verdict recorded with `rebrew test --json`.

Decision: continuing TL reconstruction. No GA was run.

with `jb` and stores the middle-loaded sum at w-0x20, so the edit uses unsigned

### 2026-11-01 — GoldTL `0x448360` scene loader body: geometry slot reuse

`src/Develop/Units/d3/GOLDTL.fcn_00448360.c` moved from 132/1406 to 771/1406
with the object at 1406 bytes, the reference size exactly (was 1353, 53 short).
Still `STUB`, no claim of a byte match.

Three source changes, each measured with
`rebrew test ... --va 0x00448360 --size 1406 --no-promote`:

- `dim` and `k` reuse `index` and `count`. The native frame proves one slot per
  pair: `0x44847f` takes `&dim` at `[esp+0x10]` and `0x44852c` writes `index` to
  the same slot; `0x4485b8` writes `k` to the slot `0x448647` later takes
  `&count`. 132 → 223, object 1376.
- The geometry rows are addressed as `g_1041d80 + index * 0x60 + n` instead of
  a `row` pointer. The native recomputes `index * 0x60` per store
  (`0x44854c`, `0x44859c`) and uses absolute bases, because all four callee-saved
  registers are taken. 223 → 259, object 1397.
- The inner six-entry loop reads both floats into one scratch float, as the
  native does: `0x4485c7` and `0x4485f7` take the address of the same local
  (`lea eax, [esp+0x28]` and `lea eax, [esp+0x30]`, one slot at `-0x124`),
  instead of reusing `fog_a`/`fog_b`. 259 → 771, object 1406.

with its objdump listing (the 771/1406 build), `.scratch/cfgslots.py` (CFG-aware

### 0x00449630 `fcn_00449630` frame and conversion scratch

- `p34` declared `float[4]` but only elements 0..2 are used: `float p34[3]`.
  Local frame drops 0x58 -> 0x54, matching the native (`sub esp, 0x54`).
- The two mouse-delta divisions were converted through explicit float casts,
  which made MSVC 6 emit a signed integer divide against a 4-byte scratch. The
  native instead converts both operands to double and stores the unsigned
  operand with a `fild qword` of a stack scratch:
  `f04 = dx / (double) w`, `a18[0] = (double) dy / f10`, and the `r` divisor
  `(double) w`. That reproduces the native's `fild qword [esp+0x28]` /
  `fidiv`-free block order and materializes `f10` at `[esp+0x20]`.
- Verification: `.venv/bin/rebrew test src/Develop/Unassigned/GOLDTL.fcn_00449630.c
  --va 0x00449630 --size 1131 --no-promote` reports match 411/1131 (was 356/1133),
  object 1127 bytes, frame 0x54. Remaining blocker: `a18` still lands at frame
  offset 0x24 rather than the native 0x18, so `p28`/`p34` sit 4 bytes high.
  Rejected (no code change or worse): union/double `a18`, `a18[3]`/`a18[4]`,
  declaration and zero-init reordering, `f10`/`f14` as double, uninitialized
  4th call argument (native reads `[esp+0x34]`, never written).

## 2026-11-01: 0x56caf0 state dispatch corrected, zero-register blocker re-established

- `0x0056caf0` (STUB, 171/896, object 896 bytes): the jump table at `0x56ce54` indexes
  `state + 2` and routes `-2` to the release body `0x56ce40`, `-1` to the queue body
  `0x56cb25`, `0` to the search body `0x56cb4b`, `1` to the removal body `0x56cc72`,
  `2` to the re-resolve body `0x56cdb2`, and `3` to the plain epilogue `0x56ce49`.
  The committed body had those labels shifted by one (queue on `0`, search on `1`,
  removal on `2`, re-resolve on `3`). The body now uses the native labels in native
  source order and reaches `cmp eax,5` with a six-entry table, matching the reference
  dispatch. Byte match stays 171/896 and content-aligned instructions stay 196/284;
  the change fixes semantics, not the metric.
- Why it cannot move yet: the reference prologue is `xor edi,edi` (2 bytes) plus
  `mov [esp+0x14],edi` (4 bytes) where the candidate emits `mov dword ptr [esp+0x10],0`
  (8 bytes). That single store puts every later byte 2 to 3 bytes off, so positional
  byte matching cannot recover even where the bodies agree instruction for instruction
  (the search body is 295 bytes in both files).
- Zero register trigger, measured: MSVC 6 /O2 does coalesce two zero stores to an
  address-taken local into one constant register and then reuses it for `push`
  arguments. A six-line helper with a copied request struct reproduces the reference
  idiom exactly (`xor edi,edi`, `mov %edi,0x70(%esp)`, `push %edi` four times). The
  switch-split layout here never triggers it. Rechecked negative: a `zero` local routed
  through every zero argument and store (folded to immediates), `found` routed through
  the same sites (folded), `int`/`char*` cast forms, declaration order permutations,
  declaration initializers, extra zero pushes in one block (up to 15), and per-run
  `/Oa`, `/Ow`, `/Ob1`, `/O1`, `/Os`. `/Oa` moves the state load to `edi` instead;
  `/O1` and `/Os` add a frame pointer, which the reference does not have.
- Slot colours: the reference wants `best` at `esp+0x10`, `found` at `esp+0x14`, the
  search counter at `esp+0x18`, and the removal counter reusing `esp+0x10`. A
  loop-condition form (`for (e = a0 + 0xac, n = 0; rec != 0 && n < 0x10; n++, e += 4)`)
  reproduces those colours and the bounded `cmp [esp+0x10],0x10; jge` loop, but emits
  908 bytes and scores 90/908, so the countdown form stays.
- Evidence: `rebrew binary asm show 0x0056caf0 --size 896`, `rebrew diff --json`
  instruction lists, `rebrew test ... --no-promote` (`STUB 171/896`), a
  `difflib.SequenceMatcher` pass over masked instruction text (196/284), and the
  `0x476a00` helper reproduction compiled with the pinned toolchain.
- Decision: user request. Verified: compile via the Rebrew cl driver, `rebrew test`
  on the file, no other source touched.

- Wrapping the rest of a function in the `else` of the first guard flips c2 block

  left operands).

  clamp ladder with `fld st(0); fld [C]; fcompp` (`0x452C60`, `0x453470`).

## 2026-11-01: 0x56caf0 case order, ascending report loop, prologue zero register (no byte gain)

- `0x0056caf0` (STUB, 171/896, object 896 bytes). Working-tree case order is already
  the native body order: the jump table at `0x56ce54` indexes `state + 2` and routes
  0 to the queue body `0x56cb25`, 1 to search `0x56cb4b`, 2 to removal `0x56cc72`,
  3 to re-resolve `0x56cdb2`, and -1/-2 to the shared release `0x56ce40`. No body
  move was needed. The stale block comment that still described the older label
  shift was corrected to the native mapping; comment text only, no code change.
- Ascending report loop, measured. `for (n = 0; n < 0x10; n++)`, `for (;;)` with a
  top `break`, `do/while`, `<= 0xf`, a `long` counter, a variable limit, and a
  `goto` loop all compile to the same rotated down-counter as the committed
  `while (n < 0x10)`, so the byte count and match stay at 896 and 171. The native
  bounded loop (`cmp [esp+0x10],0x10; jge`, counter in memory) is reproducible only
  from a loop condition that the optimizer cannot rotate, for example
  `while (rec != 0 && n < 0x10)`. That form also produces the native slot colours
  (`best` 0x10, `found` 0x14, search counter 0x18) but the object grows to 908
  bytes and the scored match drops to 90/908, so it was reverted.
- Zero register: not triggered. With the native slot colours in place the prologue
  is `mov dword [esp+0x14],0` (8 bytes) where the reference has `xor edi,edi` plus
  `mov [esp+0x14],edi` (6 bytes). The non-rotated form gives the two zero memory
  stores the reference has (`found = 0`, `n = 0`) and still folds both to
  immediates, which reproduces the earlier finding that two zero stores alone are
  not enough in this switch-split layout. Hoisting `n = 0` into the entry block
  does not help: the store is sunk back to the case that reads it.
- Blocker: the prologue byte shape, the slot colours, and the non-rotated report
  loop are one dependency chain. Any fix for the prologue needs the non-rotated
  loop, which costs 12 bytes; without a zero register those 12 bytes cannot be
  recovered, and the 2-byte prologue difference shifts every later byte so no body
  edit can score.
- Evidence: `rebrew binary asm show 0x0056caf0 --size 896 --json`,
  `rebrew build driver cl -- ... /Fo<obj>` plus `objdump -d` for eight source
  variants held in `.scratch/f56caf0/`, `rebrew test ... --no-promote --json`
  (171/896 for the countdown variants, SIZE_MISMATCH 90/908 for the bounded
  variants), and loop-idiom probes compiled with the pinned toolchain.
- Decision: keep the comment correction only; every measured variant was worse.
  No GA, no whole build.

## 2026-11-01: 0x453d80 particle emitter, three of four size regions (733/1737)

- `0x00453d80` (SIZE_MISMATCH, 326/1745, object 1743) had four size regions and a
  1-byte prologue shift that misaligned every later byte. Two were fixed from
  source evidence in the native stream.
- Statement order: the reference calls `rand()` for `p+0x0c`, then interleaves the
  `i % cnt` idiv before finishing that field, then stores `dl` to `p+0x50`
  (`0x453ed8`-`0x453efd`). The source had the two statements swapped; swapping
  them back (`p+0x0c` before `p+0x50`) is what the native scheduler produced.
- `q` alias removed. `q[8..10] += dt * s[n]` kept a second live pointer, so `p`
  spilled to `[esp+0x24]` and was reloaded before the three updates; the reference
  addresses `[esi+0x20]` directly. Writing the updates through `p` keeps the
  particle pointer in `esi`, which is also what makes the compiler save the flag
  byte (`mov al,[esi+0x51]; test al,1; mov [esp+0x54],al`) exactly as the
  reference does at `0x453e2e`-`0x453e33`.
- `cnt = 1` after the early return instead of before it: the reference emits
  `cmp [edi+0x24],ebx` and an 8-byte immediate store, which needs the constant not
  already live in `eax` for the shared `return 1` tail. `return cnt;` was tried
  first and constant-folded back to the shared form.
- Measured: 733/1737 (`rebrew test --va 0x00453d80 --size 1745 --no-promote`),
  from 326/1743. Byte-aligned comparison (`.scratch/453d80/cmp.py`) rises from
  1383 to 1466 matched bytes.
- Remaining 8 bytes, both register-allocation artifacts, not yet reproduced:
  the prologue early return is still a shared `mov eax,1` tail (`je rel32` into
  the epilogue) where the reference inlines `pop edi; mov al,1; pop ebx; add
  esp,0x40; ret` (4 bytes, `0x453d9a`-`0x453da1`); and the `dt` qword zero-extend
  stores `[esp+0x3c]` from the known-zero register (`mov [esp+0x3c],edx`, 4 bytes)
  where the reference materialises `mov dword [esp+0x3c],0` (`0x45407b`). Forcing
  either needs `edx`/`ecx` zero-register assignment to change; `unsigned int
  elapsed`, `> 0` instead of `!= 0`, dropping the redundant cast and an if/else
  form of `cnt = 1` all compiled to identical bytes or worse (`elapsed` scored
  297/1738).
- Evidence: `rebrew binary asm show 0x00453d80 --size 1745 --json`,
  `rebrew build driver cl -- ... /Fo<obj>` plus `objdump -d` for the variants in
  `.scratch/453d80.*.c`, `.scratch/453d80/cmp.py`, and the sweeps in
  `.scratch/453d80/sweep.py` / `sweep2.py`. No GA, no whole build, no verify.

## 2026-11-01: 0x45ce90 saved byte in ebp (125/264 to RELOC 264/264)

- `0x0045ce90` (SIZE_MISMATCH, 125/264, object 262) missed `push ebp`/`pop ebp`
  around the tile dispatch block. The reference keeps the saved
  `g_6b7ff8` byte in `ebp` (`push ebp; mov ebp,[esp+0x14]` at `0x45cef9`) and
  hoists `mov edx,[0x67bd2c]` between the flag mask and its application, so
  `edx` is live at the saved-byte reload and the allocator has to use `ebp`.
- Fix: an initialised declarator at the top of that block,
  `int val = g_67bd2c;`, passes `val` to `fcn_00436ff0` instead of reading the
  global inside the argument list. The added live value reproduces the whole
  reference register assignment (saved in `ebp`, global in `edx`, `x60` reloaded
  into `edx`, post-call `x68` in `eax`).

## 2026-11-01 — pragma and literal levers across six rows

- `#pragma optimize("y", off)` was the wrong assumption on two rows: under /Oy- VC6
  diverts an aligned aggregate into a dynamic frame chain instead of emitting the
  native `and esp,-8` after `mov ebp,esp`. Removing it fixed `0x4AD2E0` (34 -> 101)
  and `0x4AD6A0` (57 -> 367).
- Address-cast float constants replaced by their literal values emit the reference
  x87 form: `57.2957763671875f` (180/pi) for `0x4441C0` (147 -> 183), `0.0f`/`1.03`
  for `0x48C5B0` (150 -> 158).
- `0x547770` 404 -> 487: the same wrong pragma, the two `rep stosd`-zeroed 33-int
  arrays, and the year-mod-5 dispatch decoded from the native block extents.
- `0x43C640` 343 -> 391 and `0x5B6300` 43 -> 269 after the frame layout was
  recovered from the chkstk argument (0x1a4c) and the first cell loop written in
  native shape.

Walls measured and recorded: aligned-aggregate frames round to a multiple of 8, so
a native frame of 4 mod 8 (`0x51AF00`, `0x332c`) cannot be reproduced; `0x4DCF50`
needs its slot map rebuilt (0x170 framed bytes with no reference); `0x4DA690`
needs constant-size `rep movs` bodies before offsets align.

Pads retuned against fresh objects (2 pads, shift 0x4E0). Rebuild 2,977,792 bytes,
raw 267,667, informative 129,277, no compile or link errors.

Decision: continuing. No GA was run.

## 2026-11-02 GoldTL 0x005b6300: chkstk frame and epilogue matched

`fcn_005b6300` compiled with a 0x1a58 chkstk allocation (three spill slots) and
ended with `return 0`, while the native body allocates 0x1a4c and tail-calls
0x532ef0 after `add esp,0x1a60`. The spill came from keeping `row` and `book`
as standalone locals plus a pointer temp for the row walk; the native code
reloads `f.row`/`f.book` and parks that temp in the dead `f.v10` slot, and uses
`f.v2c` as the two-pass dispatch-loop counter.

Edits: drop the `row` and `book` locals (use the frame fields), move the first
`*a1` read above the frame initialisers, walk the hover rows through `f.v10`,
turn the dispatch outer loop into `do { } while (--f.v2c)`, and end with
`return fcn_00532ef0()`.

Evidence: `objdump -d` on the rebuilt object shows `mov eax,0x1a4c` before the
chkstk call and the `add esp,0x1a60` / `jmp` tail. `rebrew test --va 0x005b6300
--size 5499 --no-promote` reports SIZE_MISMATCH with 490 matching bytes (was
408) and a 5351-byte object. Backups and receipts under `.scratch/b6300/`.
Decision: reconstruction session. Verified: compile plus byte comparison.

  reusing the dead `f.v10` slot for a walk pointer, turning a dispatch loop into
  `do { } while (--f.v2c)`, splitting `book` so its spill disappears, and returning
  `fcn_00532ef0()` as a tail call (native `add esp,0x1a60 / jmp`). Callees reached by
  the new message loop got placeholders in `stubs/goldtl/link_scaffold.c`.
- `0x51C840` rebuilt from the candidate body: the done block with `strlen` guard and
  `strcat` is back, `fcn_0064d530(buf, p, 0x17c0)` replaces an inlined copy, and the
  prologue initialiser order matches. Instruction identity 53.9% -> 57.2% aligned,
  75.2% as a multiset, against a score that masked switch-table bytes inflate.
- `0x42BF20` txt_OpenText 1317 -> 1420: ten per-site fail epilogues inlined with only
  the shared free tail kept, and `int v30` added for the one read at 0x42d2d0.
- `0x4DCF50` 1645 -> 1646: the 0x170 of apparent slack is one `char buf[0x1f0]`
  ending exactly at the 0x760 frame, so no statements exist for the split region.

## 2026-11-02 — dialog parser loop rotation

- `0x51C840` 909 -> 918 with the object at 6043 bytes against native 6048. The loop
  is rotated (`body:` label, case ends `goto body;`, only the strlen path falls to
  the guard), `i = 0` moved into the init block, and seven copy sites converted to
  `memcpy(dst, src, strlen(src))`, which inlines to the native rep-movsd/rep-movsb
  core (16-18 rep sites now, 4 before). Conversions must be applied one site at a
  time: installing all at once drops aligned identity to 1348/1874 because the
  choices interact through register allocation.
- Normalized identity: bag 1517/1874 (80.9%), aligned 1193/1874 (63.7%), up from
  1409 and 1074.

## 2026-11-02 — append-text directives and the loop tail

- `0x519190` io_AppendText: every case label was one ASCII character off the
  native directive tables (jump targets at 0x51AE3C, 0x53-byte index at 0x51AEA4,
  default 0x19, indexed by directive-0x25). Corrected to B, R/r, E, fmt, k/s, S, v,
  h, H, e, u, l, W, V, t, T, a, A, d, D, M, `, q, C, F, %. The same pass verified
  the body errors: fmt gates on v30 not v2c, the v index is c*189*4, F's index is
  b*14+0x48e, S passes the byte at 0x773D75, C's sprintf writes work+4, h needs the
  thousands separator, and the u/t/T block ends `text_index = v0c - 1`.
- `0x51C840` 918 -> 977: the loop tail written `if (i < strlen(buf)) continue; break;`
  keeps the shared loop test instead of peeling it, giving the native head
  (`je done / cmp ebp,0x17D0 / jg done / mov edi,[esp+0x10] / body`) and the unsigned
  `jb` on the strlen path. The case-exit index `k` was corrected for the u and B
  cases only, because changing all five moves the switch tables off native offsets.
- `0x46C5A0` is ~40 instructions short of native; a continuation is transcribing them.

Decision: continuing. No GA was run.

## 2026-11-02 — GOLDTL 0x005ba910 frame scaffolding

Decision owner: reconstruction session for row 0x005ba910 (T&L trade and
transport inventory panel controller). Source:
`src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/GOLDTL.fcn_005ba910.c`.

Native facts read from `rebrew binary asm show 0x005BA910 --size 11948`:
frameless `__chkstk` frame 0x1848, saved ebx/ebp/esi/edi, arg1 at 0x1858 and
arg2 at 0x1860 (two arguments, cdecl), 3413 instructions, 265 call sites over
92 callees, 69 backward branches.

Change: the previous ten-byte stub (compiled frame 0x38) was replaced by a
frame-struct declaration and the reconstructed prologue, init block, the
`a2 & 8` branch, and the seven-iteration per-entity row loop. The frame struct
carries the native extents (scalars 0x10..0x158, int[7] at 0xd4, int[7] at
0xf0, int[9] at 0x10c, struct 0xb4 at 0x15c, 0xe28 at 0x7b0, two 0x100 objects
at 0x15d8/0x16d8, int[28] at 0x17d8) so the object reproduces the 0x1848
`__chkstk` value while the body is incomplete. Unused members are kept alive by
one volatile store at the end of the function; MSVC 6 drops unreferenced
locals, which is why a plain declaration list cannot hold the frame.

Verification: `.venv/bin/rebrew test
src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/GOLDTL.fcn_005ba910.c --va 0x005BA910 --size
11948 --no-promote --json` reports SIZE_MISMATCH with match_count 71 of 11948
(previous baseline 10) and object size 520.

Gap: the first divergence is offset 11, the saved-register sequence. Native
saves ebx/ebp/esi/edi and keeps `ebp` as the zero register and `esi` for arg1;
a truncated body leaves ebx free for the zero constant and only ebx/edi are
saved. That assignment is a whole-function decision and is expected to
converge only when the remaining region bodies exist. Native locals are
separate; the frame struct is scaffolding to be replaced as the body grows.

The subsequent locked, all-target case-normalization reconciliation reached a
stable snapshot but refused the preview because source/include contexts remain
incomplete. The earlier audit identifies many missing standard or SDK includes
in vendored library contexts, alongside parse errors; those findings require
review and cannot be assumed irrelevant to every symbol. Receipt:
`.scratch/counter-contract/vfs-normalize-locked-run2.log`. No binding changed.

## 2026-11-02 — GOLDTL 0x005ba910 packet builder and entity-slot init

Decision owner: reconstruction session for row 0x005ba910. Source:
`src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/GOLDTL.fcn_005ba910.c`.

Change: transcribed the native body after the init block, in native order,
0x5bab17 through 0x5baf75. The `0x77531c` clear moved to its native place, the
`0x868050 + idx + idx*0x24c` row pointer and the four packet-builder arms
(`fcn_00502cd0` rows 0xff/0x2a/0x116/0x1db/0x1dc) replaced the placeholder, the
`*(unsigned short*)packet` header word now indexes `0x99ec10` into the 0x41-byte
record table, the 16-slot 0xf0-stride slot clear is written out, and the
`fcn_0057e880`/`fcn_00470820`/`fcn_00471b60`/`d2_SetForm` window open plus the
`fcn_00533a60` row-id layout and the a2/0x774970 selection arms are in place.

Frame facts recovered with a CFG-aware push-depth propagation (no conflicting
depths over all 3413 instructions): the frame base is the post-`__chkstk` esp,
arg1/arg2 at 0x184c/0x1850, the 16 entity slots are 0xf0 apart starting at 0x6d8
(the 0xe28 extent at 0x7b0 is slot 0 + 0xd8, not a separate local), and the two
0x100 objects at 0x15d8/0x16d8 abut the slot array. The frame struct was recut
to that layout (`Ent5ba910` slots replace the former 0xe28 blob). Native stores
`a2 & 1` once per outer arm and tests the memory slot again later; writing it as
`f.v70 = a2 & 1` keeps MSVC from spilling a fourth value, which is what pins the
struct to frame offset 0.

Verification: `.venv/bin/rebrew test
src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/GOLDTL.fcn_005ba910.c --va 0x005BA910 --size
11948 --no-promote --json` reports SIZE_MISMATCH with match_count 120 of 11948
(previous 71), object size 1533 (previous 520), and the frame immediate back to
0x1848 with zero struct displacement. The first divergence is offset 11: native
loads arg1 into esi and keeps ebp as the zero register, this build loads arg2
into esi and keeps ebx as zero. That assignment is a whole-body decision.

Gap: the body is transcribed to 0x5baf75 of 0x5bd7bb. The remaining region
floats, `io_AppendText` id blocks and the SEH arm stay out.

  instead of falling through.
- `0x519190` frame is now measured exactly from the /Z7 s-bp records: our homes are
  text_index 0x08, digit 0x1c, v14 0x28 and so on, while native's are 0x0c, 0x1c? no,
  digit 0x0c, ap 0x10, v0c 0x18, v14 0x20, v1c 0x28, v20 0x2c, v30 0x3c, v2c 0x38,
  directive 0x33. Native's assignment order differs, so a 13th slot alone cannot
  reproduce displacements: the third push and the slot order are both needed. The
  preamble is 0x23 bytes shorter because native inlines four early-return epilogues
  (nine total) while ours shares one, and native inlines the strcpy at 0x519266.
  Block order deviates in two places: fmt belongs right after case S, and the
  continue target is the loop head.

## 2026-11-02: fcn_005ba910 init order moved ahead of v10C block

`GOLDTL.fcn_005ba910.c` set the `f.vF0[]` message-id constants after the `f.vD4[]`
`-1` run. The host compiler hoists the two `0x93` stores (`f.v10C[8]` and
`f.vF0[2]`) as a shared-constant pair, so their position in the source moves the
early byte stream. Moving the seven `f.vF0[]` stores to just after `f.v88 = 0;`
moved that pair later and raised the stored match from 772 to 782 bytes with the
object size unchanged at 12365 (native 11948). Frame stays 0x1848 and the
`xor eax,eax; add esp,0x1858; ret` epilogue is unchanged. Probes that removed
either `0x93` store, assigned `f.vF0[2]` from `f.v10C[8]`, or moved the
`f.v14 = a1` store scored lower (713 to 794 without the store, which is not a
permitted source state) and were reverted; scratch copies and the measurement
JSON live in `.scratch/5ba910/`.

## 2026-11-02 — find loop base rematerialisation in the type scan

`0x547770` 731 to 760 with the object at 5566 against native 5595. The promotion of n7b into
ebx is driven by whether the count loop references the `tb` source variable: when the loop
computes the record base from the global directly (`q = *(u8**)0x868050 + *rp + *rp*0x24c`,
no `tb`), MSVC 6 promotes n7b and emits native's prologue (push ebx, push ebp, xor ebx,ebx,
push esi, cmp ecx,4, push edi, then the clamp's store order), giving match 760. Assigning
tb inside the loop body compiles to the same object but the compiler does not hoist the load
(per-iteration `mov ecx,[0x868050]`), while hoisting through any local pointer (tb or a
separate base) puts the load back in a register, re-spills n7b and returns to 731. The object
is 29 bytes short and the slot map is still off (n7a 0x28 against 0x10, thr 0x20 against 0x28,
fild temp 0x18 against 0x14, mask still a stack slot where native keeps it in ebx); declaration
order is not the lever, only the initialiser store order swaps n7a and n7b.

## 2026-11-02 — trade ai remainder idiom decoded

The wall at offset 0xb0 is decoded and reproduced. Native's bytes at 0x489b20 are
`mov eax,ds:0x7f4c04; and 0xffff; and 0x80000001; jns; dec; or 0xfffffffe; inc; je`, which is not
a bit test: `and 0xffff` narrows the dividend to unsigned short, `and 0x80000001` keeps sign and
parity, `jns` tests the sign flag of that result, and `dec`/`or 0xfffffffe`/`inc` convert sign plus
parity into the signed remainder, so the `je` branches on remainder zero. Because the dividend is
already 16-bit, the sign chain is unreachable and the value is `x & 1`. The source form is
`if ((*(int*)0x7f4c04 & 0xffff) % 2) { if ((*(int*)(o+0x1b4) & 0x200) == 0) {...} *(int*)(o+0x1b4) |= 0x200; } else { *(int*)(o+0x1b4) &= ~0x200; }`,
truthy test with the odd arm first, because an `== 0` test with the clear arm first emits `jne`
where native has `je`. With it the first mismatch moves from 0xb0 to 0xc8 and match rises from 605
to 638; the object grows to 6082 because the price body 0xde..0x461 runs 40 bytes longer than
native's 0xde..0x439 (the set and clear at 0x461 are byte-identical to native's 0x439 shifted by
0x28) while later regions are 13 bytes shorter, netting +27. Kept for the decoded construct, with
the body gap as the open item; fixture k_6082_638.c is the current source.

## 2026-11-02 — task dispatcher frame solved

`0x4D8D00` 318 to 329 with the frame now native at 0x138 and the object 4396, msg still at 0x30
against native 0x3c. One line did the frame: `char b118[0x30]` instead of 0x20. The premise that
the four buffers overlapped by 0x10 was wrong, and the frame formula settles it: in this build
`sub esp` equals max_local_end minus 0x10 because the saved registers occupy slots 0x00..0x10 and
locals start at 0x10, so native's 0x138 pins max_local_end to 0x148; no native access exists in
0x138..0x148, and b118 at 0x118 must therefore be 0x30. The buffers total 0xc0 in a tight
0x88..0x148 region, and the measured slot chain with that size is contiguous. The slot map is now
v10 0x10, v14 0x14, base 0x18, tgt 0x1c, ent 0x20, v28 0x28, v80 0x2c, msg 0x30, vec 0x5c,
i 0x6c, v68 0x70, v84 0x74, be8 0x88, bb8 0xb8, b88 0xe8, b118 0x118, where native has ent 0x18,
base 0x1c, tgt 0x20, v24 0x24, v28 0x28, vec 0x2c, msg 0x3c, v68 0x68, i 0x6c, temps 0x70/0x78,
v80 0x80, v84 0x84 and the buffers from 0x88. Blocking msg at 0x3c, all measured as no-ops:
declaration permutations of all four buffers, msg/vec swap, base/ent swap, moving v80/v84 down the
list, block-scoping msg and vec into the loop, and early live vec writes before the loop.
Declaration order has zero effect on slot assignment here; scalars do respond to first-assignment
order (prologue `v80 = 0; v84 = 0;` moves v80 to 0x28 and swaps v10/v14), and msg at 0x3c needs vec
assigned first, which the allocator refuses because arrays slot at first use and msg's rep movsl is
first. The object is 244 bytes short while emitting 1541 instructions against native's 1452, so
ours has more, smaller instructions and the remaining slot order is driven by that code shape
rather than by declarations.

## 2026-11-02 — dispatcher prologue register documented

`0x4D8D00` keeps 616 at object 4640 with call counts 11/9/16 and ent34 at 25 sites; the
register-plan pass was negative and the source is restored byte-identical to the kept state. At
offset 12 we emit `xor ebx,ebx` where native has `xor edx,edx`, and the slots differ (ours base
0x18, ent 0x1c, vec 0x5c, msg 0x30, v80 0x2c, v68 0x70; native ent 0x18, base 0x1c, vec 0x2c, msg
0x3c, v80 0x80, v68 0x68). The mechanism: our v68 stays in ebx for its whole live range, so its
zero is callee-saved and i needs a second scratch zero in eax, while native keeps v68
memory-resident ([esp+0x68] = edx at 0x4d8d17, reloaded into ebx at 0x4d9ce3) so its zero is
scratch edx CSE'd with i's zero. Every lever that pushes v68 into memory also merges one
fcn_004c6940 tail: address-taking it in a call argument moves the first mismatch to 13 and swaps
ent/base to native order but costs one c6940 (15) with proxy match 204 to 227; volatile v68 gives
4652 with c6940 15 and first 13; v68 as a struct member gives 4648 with c67c0 8 and c6940 15; and
base-before-v68 store order, `(void)&v68`, self-reads, long or unsigned forms, predicate zeros and
loop pointer rewrites are all identical to the base. Recorded in docs/codegen-walls.md: the next
lever is the twelve-instruction delta (native 1452 against our 1464), which is what would change
register pressure enough to spill v68 like the reference.

## 2026-11-02 — formatter copy tails measured against the register cap

`0x51AF00` keeps the nested skeleton at 888 match and object 6455; the copy-tail round produced no
keeper and the source is unchanged. The cap is the missing ebx save: the loop index lives in esi
where native saves ebx, esi and edi (chkstk 0x3330 against native 0x332c), and since every inlined
rep movs clobbers esi, i is spilled and reloaded around each copy tail while a case-local k lands
in edx and is stored and reloaded around the memmove. That accounts for the +12 bytes and +5
instructions on u/U/b/B/e/E and the a/T/w gaps; `register int i` is byte-identical and moving i's
declaration to the top is byte-identical. The per-case extent misattribution is cross-jump
placement, not body size: native T's 138 is its own 49-byte body plus a-path2's 89-byte tail since
T falls through, and native a's two tails live in T's and D's buckets at 0x51b98f and 0x51c100,
while ours shares the group and owns it from a, so T -70 against a +123 is one fact. Tail edits at
6455 all measured worse: a copies through strcpy 6555/799, a literal expressions 6535/804, a with
strlen temporaries 6527/808, D with cp_n 6471/837, w with a literal memcpy 6495/842, T+a+D
6479/812, the u rewrite 6447/817, and w with u/U/b/B/e rewrites 6259/785 where the identical

## 2026-11-03 — trade name dialog aggregate promotion documented

`0x5B7880` keeps 299 at object 3980 with the equal prefix at 76 bytes; the follow-up pass produced no
keeper and the source is unchanged. The cause of the 0x4c mismatch is aggregate promotion, not the -1
initialiser form: native keeps f.win in EDI across calls, storing it to frame+0x10 at 0x78fb and then
using `mov [edi+0x228]` sites with no reload, while our single FRAME aggregate reloads f.win from the
frame at every use, leaving EDI free so the sentinel takes it (`or edi,-1` at 0x4b against native's
`or ebp,-1`). MSVC 6 will not promote a struct member once any member's address is taken, and our source
passes &f.msg to memset and fcn_004c5530 and &f.rows[0] to the pointer walk; scratch probes confirm a
clean aggregate promotes its member to edi while the same aggregate with those addresses taken does not.
Splitting the frame into CTL (15 scalars, 0x3c) plus DATA (msg through old, 0x10d0) restores promotion
and the correct CTL offsets (nSlots 0x30, hA 0x0c, hB 0x18, hC 0x1c, hD 0x24, hRadio 0x2c, ent 0x28) but
gives frame 0x1110 with DATA at 0x40 (txtName lea at [esp+0x598] against native 0x594), one extra 4-byte
slot between the two, and win in EBX with ent in EDI and the sentinel in EAX. A win alias keeps frame
0x110c but steals ESI from a0 and moves the prologue push, regressing the prefix. The same cause accounts
for most of the +186 bytes: about 18 f.win reloads plus non-CSE'd GUI(f.rows[i].label) control-index
recomputations, where native computes the label index once at 0x7bf9 with shl/sub/lea and two stores.

## 2026-11-03 — trade dialog prologue cascade blocked

`0x5B88B0` keeps 404 at object 4300 with frame 0x1368 and the first mismatch at 23, where native loads
the base into edx and we use ebp. The pass confirmed the earlier findings and produced no keeper. The
byte-typed prototype costs: `int __cdecl fcn_0050b750(int, unsigned char)` alone gives object 4290 with
match 238 and the same first mismatch, and adding `unsigned char*` for a0 gives 4291 with match 255.
Moving the top store to nSlots gives objects 4294 or 4295 with frame 0x136c and the base load in edi, and
pkt 0xfc brings the frame back to 0x1368. The blocker is the register cascade: on msvc-6.0-sp5-pp the base
load never reaches edx and exactly one of the five -1 stores is always sunk, whatever the source shape.
Tested: six store orders (plain, chained, declaration initialisers, struct temp plus copy, nSlots-1
sentinels, a shared negated variable, and all 15 scalars as a struct in native slot order with textual
field rewrite); ent spellings (void pointer, int, unsigned casts, operand order, the sibling 0x506380
form, two-step, register locals, base in tv, char pointer ent, unsigned sentinels); parameter and
prototype shapes; and pre-call uses or guards, all folded. Volatile is the only construct that forces
the stores but it emits `mov dword ptr [esp+..],0xffffffff` for eight bytes instead of a four-byte
register store: volatile hD with nSlots and pkt 0xfc gives frame 0x1368, object 4300, first mismatch 22
and match 428, the only candidate above 404, while volatile hA gives 4314, sel 4340, hB 4302, hC 4310
and all six 4367. The native cascade ent to eax, -1 to ebx, 0 to ebp and base to edx follows from -1
living in ebx, which only happens when the lea chain owns eax at materialisation time, and every source

## 2026-11-03 — inventory dialog merge is register pressure, source clean

`0x5D0660` keeps its v14 state at 1258 with object 4389, frame 0x438, nine store blocks and lint clean; the
merge round produced no keeper and the source is byte-identical to kept-v14. The shared visibility block is
reproducible but the compensation pool cannot pay for it. The duplicate exists because of register pressure
rather than source shape: both tabB[2] arms already write identical statements, but native spills n3 to its
slot, freeing ebx and edi so the label text stays in a callee-saved register and the id index lands in esi at
both sites, while our build keeps n3 in ebx so the else arm reloads tabB[2].text and puts the id index in
edi, and MSVC's suffix merge therefore sees different register streams. Forcing n3 to memory reproduces
native's merge exactly, either as `volatile int n3` or through an address-taken use: eight store blocks, the
else arm jumping into the tabB[3] store tail at the native-relative spot, and the preludes `mov eax,reg; add
esp,0x10; shl eax,6; sub eax,reg`, with frame 0x438 held. Measured, all at frame 0x438: volatile n3 gives
object 4345 with eight stores and match 560; an address-taken n3 gives 4330, eight stores, match 430; that
plus eight sentinel conversions gives 4359, eight stores, match 556; a tabA[0] plus else sentinel variant
gives 4393 with nine stores and match 822; tabA[0] and tabA[1] reading .text instead of the temp gives 4359
with nine stores and match 376; and the volatile variant plus that tabA change gives 4335, eight stores,
match 392. The merge costs 33 to 44 bytes rather than 32, since the tabB[3] tail plus the else tail is 0x47
in native against 0x68 here, and the nine `cmp word ptr [mem],0xffff` sites are worth one byte each, about
14 in one build, leaving a merged object still 24 to 30 short with no byte-neutral compensation: volatile nb
or idx break the frame at 0x43c and volatile t0 gives 4538 while still merging. The rest of the deficit sits
in the tabA label blocks, where native stores .text before the branch and spills t0 and n3, and touching
those cascades through the allocation. The kept body has 1104 strictly equal bytes with the longest equal run
54 bytes at 0x154, so the match is spread over small runs and any global allocation change loses more than
the localized win. Recommendation: rebuild the pre-merge label blocks (tabA[0] and tabA[1], native
0x5d08e9..0x5d09cf, 17 and 6 bytes over ours) before landing the merge. Merged candidates are kept in
.scratch/660/r11/ (e1a and e10 are the cleanest at frame 0x438 with the shared block present), with tooling in
.scratch/660/tools/ and the write-up in NOTES-rewrite.md round 6.

`0x540020` returns to NEAR_MATCHING at exactly 4393 with match 3921 (89 percent), 258 relocations, lint at

with a matched prefix of 2837 bytes. Six shapes did it. The first 0x300 loop adds 2, 4 or 8 through immediate
arms rather than an add temp. `w = (int)(fcn_0042e410(0x5a) & 0xffff); if (w > fcn_0050bfe0(obj))` replaces
the inline comparison, and that single change flipped the whole register allocation to land exactly 4393.
The raw-then-clamped store is written `*(volatile int*)((char*)obj+0x39) = v; v = v < 0 ? 0 : v;
*(volatile int*)((char*)obj+0x39) = v;` because the volatile first store defeats MSVC 6 dead-store
elimination while non-volatile int or unsigned casts are still eliminated, and the ternary supplies native's
setl, dec and and. The running remainder lives in `leftw`, derived from `fcn_0050d2a0(...) * 75` and reduced
by the ftol with a mirror into `left`, so divisions use `leftw` and the multiplicand lands in edi with
`lea eax,[edi+edi]`. `cand = -1; agebits = -1;` precede the last 0x300 loop. The last loop's store block
does `r += 0x70;` then three stores as native's `add eax,0x70` form. And the second loop tail is
`while ((obj = fcn_00503e80()) != 0)`. The remaining differences are allocation-only and net size zero: n sits
in ebx where native uses ebp, obj sits in ebp where native uses esi in the first loop, and native keeps a
float temp with `fst [esp+0x18]` before the ftol that we do not emit. New locals `leftw` and the reused `w`
are placeholders to rename under the naming conventions if they persist. Backups .scratch/f540020/kept.c and
win_4393.c hold the current source, with notes in WALK_FINDING.md.
