which turns the je into a real block join so MSVC emits separate `add esp,4` / `add esp,4` instead of merging
to `add esp,8` and the je target becomes 0xebd like native; semantics are preserved because with gebaeude==0
the compiler jumps to the shared `fcn_00546190(e); return;` tail, exactly what break did, and that was the
three-byte shortfall. Remaining and not closed: the scratch int-conversion slots at 0x537 and 0x53f are at
0x24 and 0x18 against native 0x30 and 0x24, a constant -0xc; the `xor ebx,ebx` zeroings at 0x8cc, 0x955 and
0x96b are two bytes short each and appeared only after the df local, since ours uses `test ax,ax` plus an edi
counter instead of `cmp ax,bx`; the rohstoff address fold at 0x974 emits `add eax,edx; lea esi,[eax+0x2e]`
where native is two bytes longer and both the two-way and temp-pointer source forms fold to a single lea; the
`xor ecx,ecx` before `mov cx,[ebp+0xac]` at 0xaef is two bytes short with ours using esi and eax instead of
ecx; and the tail at 0xed4 is native's 16-byte switch table plus nops which the tool strips. Constant audit
against the reference bytes: 0x665be8 is the double 0.000992063492063492 for 1.0/1008.0 so the existing
`(1.0 / 1008.0)` is right, 0x6628a8 is the double 0.0 whose dword load is the float zero, and 0x66419c is the
float 1.3f, so no constant change was needed. Current source at .scratch/he_RunProduktion.best.c and
.scratch/571870.v8.c with the helper scripts check.py, pair.py, deltamap.py, fpvar.py, fivar.py and
case2var.py.

`0x561380` goes from 14.25 to 16.22 percent (584 matching bytes) with the object at 3444 from 3404 and 48
relocations, lint clean. The whole function is transcribed in native order: the prologue `sub esp,0x5e4`,
push ebx/ebp/esi, `mov esi,[esp+0x5f4]`, `or ebx,-1`, push edi; the guard
`if (p[0xc8] != -1 && !fcn_004c4450(...)) return`; the dispatch `add eax,2; cmp 0xa; ja default;
jmp [eax*4+0x562158]` with its table decoded to eleven entries in value order -2, -2, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
pointing at 0x56212f, 0x56212f, 0x5613c5, 0x56149d, 0x5614f7, 0x56157d, 0x561817, 0x561c33, 0x5620af,
0x56169e and 0x561763; all eleven case bodies; three shared tails at 0x56148f, 0x561d51 and 0x56211d; the
case-3 pos aggregate with its out pointer read back as `*(int*)(*(uchar**)(pos+3)+4)`; the case-4
filtered-entity loop as a native do/while with `(int)` casts on both sides of the 0x85a0a4 pointer-range
compare and the 0x87*4 stride; the message and name field offsets; the case-5 name-table init from the three
64-byte literals; the fild float pos updates; the he_MessageBoxQuickjump and io_FormatTextBuffer argument
order; and the fcn_00417d00 ftol path. Every callee resolves to a project definition, with 0x64d228 as the
_ftol library row. The single blocker is the frame: target 0x5e4 against our 0x5d0. The target layout is
decoded exhaustively as 0x10 unused then three four-byte slots at 0x10, 0x14 and 0x18 (q with v10, a float,
and recB with color[4]), pos[8] at 0x1c, three char[64] at 0x3c, 0x7c and 0xbc, msg[0xf8] at 0xfc and
text[0x3f0] at 0x1f4, with 0x1f4 + 0x3f0 = 0x5e4 exactly, so `sub esp` is the 0x10 hole plus 1492. Our
compile has no leading 0x10 and only two four-byte slots for 1488, so every displacement is 0x14 low and the
prefix stalls at offset 2. Probes confirmed that slot order is strictly ascending size and contiguous, that
unused or assigned-but-unread locals get no slot, that four scalar chars pack into one four-byte slot, and
that switch scoping, fild scratch, _ftol, varargs and jump tables add no hole, so the target's 0x10 must come
from a size class below four bytes or a compiler internal reserve, and it was not reproducible from source.
Also confirmed rather than assumed: MSVC defers and merges `add esp` across consecutive calls, so the
target's deferred-pop pattern needs no special source shape, and `sub esp` equals the byte sum with no
rounding. Backups in .scratch/r561380/ (orig.c and v1_16.22.c).

## 2026-11-03 — season setup colouring measured as an order list

`0x540020` keeps its corrected state at 3872 with object 4393, 258 relocations, frame 0x3b8 and the first
mismatch at 0xb15; round four kept no edit and the tree is restored to base_v4.c. The allocator was measured
rather than guessed: the register preference order is esi, edi, ebp, ebx, with ebp preferred over ebx, which is
what makes the three-candidate cases fit, and every build fits a per-web priority list. The current state has
obj, w, leftw, n in that order giving esi, edi, ebp, ebx; dropping w's web gives obj, leftw, n for esi, edi,
ebp; divisions on left give obj, w, n; the 3921 baseline had w, leftw, obj, n for esi, edi, ebp, ebx; and
native needs obj, leftw, n, w. So w must fall from position two to last, below n, not merely below leftw, and
obj keeps esi because it inherits the register from the pre-loop walk at 0xa7b. Shapes measured inert for the
priority list with size and prefix held: a 16-bit-valued w, `unsigned short w` in a block, `short w`, w in a
nested block, renaming the loop w, renaming or splitting the early w, function-scope leftw in three
declaration positions, loop-head statement permutations (prefix 0xb0c or 0xb14), merged `left = leftw = ...`,
`75 * fcn(...)`, `2 * leftw / n`, `leftw << 1`, comparison operand order, hoisting w's definition out of the
gate block (the compiler sinks it back), a redundant `left = leftw` at the loop tail, using leftw after the
second loop (4414), splitting leftw into lwt at the second loop head, and swapping the [esi+1] and ent store
order. Making w memory-resident or inlined gives the wanted leftw in edi and n in ebp but deletes w's register
(4391 or 4400) or n's ebx, so it is not the answer. New native fact: fcn_0042e410 returns a 16-bit type, since
native emits `mov bx,ax; push esi; and ebx,0xffff; call; add esp,8; cmp eax,ebx`; declaring
`unsigned short __cdecl fcn_0042e410(int);` with `w = (int)(fcn_0042e410(0x5a) & 0xffff)` reproduces that
sequence exactly with the same scheduling but costs one byte for object 4394, which balances against leftw in
edi dropping the `+0x0` displacement that ebp forces on `lea eax,[ebp+ebp*1+0x0]` at 0xe17, so the role flip
and the 16-bit callee fix are both needed to hold 4393 and the role flip comes first. A role-normalised
structural diff of the loop shows the remaining non-register differences are only the scheduling of
`mov cl,[0x773d75]` with its and, the ENTCLASS encoding `[eax+ecx*1+0x247]` against native's
`[ecx+eax+0x247]`, and the [esi+1] load placement in the evs fill; the loop CFGs are identical with the back
edge at 0xb3b, so the colouring difference is not a CFG artifact. Artifacts: ROUND4.md with the full measured
table, roles.py, exp.py and xloop.py, plus keep_wret_tmp.c for the 4394 16-bit callee variant. Recommended
next attempt: treat the colouring as opaque and either find a shape that moves w below n, with the untested
family being a change to how n's 2/4/8 accumulation interacts with the divisor, such as accumulating a
multiplier instead of n, or accept the current roles and push on the remaining per-instruction differences.

## 2026-11-03 — inventory extents repaired where the reference tails are padding

Two extents were wrong because the inventory includes alignment nops that follow the function. Disassembly of
the reference ends 0x561380's code at 0x562184 with twelve 0x90 bytes from 0x562184 to 0x56218f, so its code
extent is 3588 rather than the inventoried 3600, and it ends 0x571870's code at 0x572758 with eight 0x90 bytes
from 0x572758 to 0x57275f, so that extent is 3816 rather than 3824. Both were repaired through
`rebrew binary repair-extents 0x561380=3588 0x571870=3816 --reason ... --sync-rows` after a preview digest of
cbd7f888f18a5d0d22da4c702e79fc7c4e570b803a0c14b0c605252db04caa81, which updated the inventory rows and synced the
function row sizes. The effect is direct and large: 0x571870 now measures 2757 matching bytes at object 3816
with size 3816, so its verdict moves from SIZE_MISMATCH to NEAR_MATCHING because the size is exact, and 0x561380
measures 1244 at object 3592 against the corrected 3588, so it is four bytes over its code extent instead of
eight. This also explains the earlier confusion where a row's object could never reach the inventoried size: the
object extent excludes trailing section padding that the inventory counts. Rows whose extent has not been
audited keep their inventoried sizes, and the same repair is the right step for any other row whose reference
tail is alignment padding.

## 2026-11-03 — extent audit classified, table tails included

The inventory audit found 151 rows whose recorded extent ends in a run of at least four 0x90 or 0xCC bytes. A
decode from each row start, resynchronising over validated four-byte jump tables, split them into 21 rows whose
code ends with a control transfer followed only by padding with the next row starting exactly at the recorded
end, 89 rows whose byte before the run is the last dword of an in-function jump table whose targets point back
into the row, and 41 rows that did not classify because of decode desync or a data tail, which stay excluded.
The classification table is .scratch/extents/classified.json. Both of the first two classes are repairs: the
criterion is that the trailing run is alignment after the function's last content, and for a switch-bearing
function that content is the jump table. The earlier filter wording that required the byte before the run not to
be table data was wrong and would have excluded the two precedent repairs, since 0x561380's table dwords end at
0x562184 with twelve nops to 0x56218f for an extent of 3588 and 0x571870's dwords end at 0x572758 with eight nops
to 0x57275f for 3816, both of which were applied. Multi-byte nop forms also count as padding, so the row
0x641810, recorded at 368 bytes with a 32-byte int3 run and a 7-byte `lea esi,[esi]` between the final ret and
that run, is repaired to 329 rather than 336. Repairs run in batches of at most eight through
`rebrew binary repair-extents 0xVA=SIZE ... --reason <evidence> --sync-rows`, with a dry run for the input digest
and then the apply guarded by `--expected-digest`, and receipts kept under .scratch/extents/.

## 2026-11-03 — crew dialog frame needs expression pressure, not declarations

`0x43C640` keeps 469 at object 5169 against native 5419 with the frame at 0x54 and the first mismatch at offset 5
where native is 0x60; the frame pass kept nothing and the source is restored to the session baseline. The tactic
of naming the two H-derived temporaries cannot work as stated: MSVC sinks a standalone `hh = t->H; hx = hh*x;`
past the following call and rematerialises `[ebx+4]` afterwards, so the named values never become live across the
RNG call and never claim slots. The frame only grows with expression-shape pressure, not declaration count, since
three unused ints leave the frame at 0x54. Measured probes, all kept as evidence and reverted from the source:
hoisting H, hx and hy before all sixteen RNG calls gives frame 0x58 at object 5335 with match 447; adding
`hz = hx + col` gives 0x5c at 5312; moving the RNG call inside the verts expression as
`... + (f = (float)fcn()*g*jx) + f ...` gives 0x58 at 5360; and volatile hh, hx and hy gives 0x5c at 5856, over
native's size. None reached 0x60 and every one lost match, so all were reverted. Two further differences were
recorded that bear on the same region: native emits the record-init loop as direct stores at material offset +0xbc
over eight strides of 0x34, where our source walks a RegionRecord pointer from +0xa0, and native's memset form
emits three rep-stos stages against our two. Both change register pressure in the region that owns native's -0x58
and -0x5c slots, so the next lever is to reproduce the region-init and scan expression shapes, namely the memset
length temporaries, the direct material-field stores and `off` held in a slot, rather than forcing the emission
temporaries. Backups in .scratch/goldtl-0043c640/ with v4-hoist.c, v5-comma.c and v6-volatile.c.

## 2026-11-03 — quest dialog low pool is claimed by address-taken-ness

`0x512EE0` keeps its state at 393 with object 3448, three relocations, frame 0x404 and lint clean; the slot pass
kept no edit. The mechanism is now known: the low pool slot is claimed by address-taken-ness, not by declaration
or emission order, since declaration permutations of inner, total and i, renames and alternate initialiser orders
are all byte-identical. Taking the address of the value that must live at 0x14 moves the prologue store there,
which matches native: its only scalar lea site is 0x13375 for `&[esp+0x14]`, and native slot 0x14 is both the
found counter and the 0x65 and 0x69 count, because native stores the fcn_0050cf50 result straight to 0x14 at
0x13367, so native merges count into the found counter and keeps no separate count variable. Measurements, all at
frame 0x404 unless noted: making both address-taken sites `&total` puts the store at 0x14 with i at 0x10, gives
total 0x14, kinds 0x18 and prefix 0x2, but its semantics are wrong at 0x65 because total does not yet hold the
fcn_0050cf50 result; splitting the sites, first `&count` then `&total`, keeps frame 0x404 and kinds 0x1c with i at
0x10, total at 0x14 and count at 0x18, and raises the prefix to 0xe9 with match 405 at object 3469, but native's
two amp leas at 0x13375 and 0x13389 both resolve to slot 0x14, so that split cannot be the original shape and is
not promoted; and the correctly merged forms, whether by renaming count to total or merging it, are semantically
right but drop i from the low pool with frame 0x400, kinds 0x18 and prefix 0x2. A third artificial address-taken
scalar restores frame 0x404 but still leaves kinds at 0x18, so the third low slot appears only when the third
scalar is itself address-taken, which native's lea inventory rules out. The conclusion is that i at 0x10 and total
at 0x14 are reachable by making total address-taken, while the third slot, inner at 0x18 in native, is a plain
register spill, and our merged-correct shape does not spill inner because our do-while register pressure is lower
than native's. The next probe is to force inner's spill inside the do-while, or find the source form where the
merged total keeps i in the pool, since the correct merged variants currently collapse to two slots at frame
0x400. Tool added: .scratch/512ee0/probe3.py reporting frame, prologue store slot, kinds start, amp slot and
prefix, with backups L3.c and pre_m11_swap.c.

the verts index, matching native's -0x10 and -0x14 slots and its H*x reload after the call; and `cells = t->H*t->H`
is a persistent local used at the memset of cand, the bestmap memcpy and the memset of map, which is the pure-C
shape that buys the third frame slot. Three findings shape the next pass. The three-stage rep-stos clear cannot be
produced from C on this profile, since ten spellings under the sp5-pp driver give the plain two-stage form, which
agrees with docs/msvc6-c-shapes.md section 11 and docs/codegen-walls.md section 6b, so native's -0x58 store and its
separate fild temp at -0x60 need reviewed assembly if they are wanted. `off` already owns a slot, so native's

v19 0x11c and v22 0x19c, so there are two pair swaps plus a difference in v13's home. Layout levers exist but
cost bytes: `char v20[16]` instead of `[14]` packs the two-byte pad and flips the aggregates exactly to v16 0x44

cases 0 and 1 plus fifteen. Declarations, element type, alignment and struct grouping are all irrelevant to the
pair order. The stronger root cause is that the frame order is downstream of where v13's home lands: the
reference keeps v13 in ebx across case 7 and spills its home only after v29 dies, so v13's home aliases v29's

init store but leaves v29 at 0x1c, so that lever does not move the pair either. The remaining route is to
reproduce the reference's allocation order for v13 and v29 from case-7 code shape, or to accept the frame order as
downstream and chase the four-byte overage through case 8 and case 9 scheduling, which are minus ten and plus nine

## 2026-11-03 — inventory switch case six merge tied to the minus-one register

`0x561380` keeps its state at 2451 with object 3584 against native 3588, 110 relocations and lint clean; the
case-6 pass kept no edit and the source is byte-identical to the v29 state. Case lengths remain 0xd8, 0x5a, 0x86,
0x121, 0xc5, 0xb4, 0x41c, 0x47c, 0x7c for cases 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 4, 5 and 6 against native 0x80 for case 6, with
the -1/-2 arm at 0x29, and the first mismatch is now offset 17 where we emit `or ebp,-1` (0xcd) and native emits
`or ebx,-1` (0xcb). The main finding is that the case-6 tail merge is not independent of case 3 but rides the same
knob as the minus-one register. Because the v29 state hoists `q = p + 0x52` above the fcn_004f4f60 call, q takes
edi across that call, r takes ebx, and the function's -1 constant is forced into ebp; with -1 in ebp the fail block
at 0x10f, which is case 0's tail, is `mov %ebp,0x70` plus the epilogue and is byte-identical to case 6's own r==0
return at 0xd42, so every fail goto including case 6's else is redirected there and case 6's je becomes the
two-byte short form for 0x7c. Every variant that leaves -1 in ebx instead gets case 6 at 0x80 with the six-byte
far je, because the canonical fail block at label_561d51 inside case 5 then starts with `or $-1,%ebx` and is not
identical to case 6's copy, so nothing is redirected: breaking the merge is the same thing as moving -1 to ebx.
The best lead measured, c3i1 in .scratch/r561380, advances the parameter destructively instead of using a q
register, `a0 = (void*)((unsigned char*)a0 + 0x52);`, which gives case 3 at 0x121, case 6 at 0x80 and -1 in ebx,
but case 5 grows to 0x47f for object 3592 and match 2315, below the current state, so it was reverted and its
first mismatch moves from offset 17 to 43. Case 5 grows because native zeroes ebx with `xor %ebx,%ebx` at 0x561cf8
since ebp holds v10, so the zeroing also kills -1 and label_561d51 becomes the seven-byte `movl $-1` at case-5
offset 0x11e for 0x47c, whereas in our builds v10 spills, ebp is free, the zero goes to ebp, ebx keeps -1 and the
fail block becomes `or $-1,%ebx` plus a late `mov %ebx,0x70` at offset 0x257 for three extra bytes. Forcing v10
into the compare with `&& v10 == 0` gives case 5 at 0x478 and moves -1 back to ebp, returning case 6 to 0x7c, so
it is not usable. The immediate-store route has no C lever on case 6's path, since the lookup call preserves ebp
so the -1 register is never clobbered there, and cases 4 and 5 get `movl $-1` only because their bodies reuse that
register before the fail. The next step is to make case 5's zero constant land in ebx while -1 stays in ebx, which
native achieves by keeping v10 in ebp. Variants c3i1, c3h1, c3g2, c3e1, c6m2, c3t1, c5v10, c3j1, c3j2 and c3j3
and notes in .scratch/r561380/NOTES_round7b.md.

fewer across the two vertex-emission segments, so 5419 cannot be reached by deleting seventy-two bytes of spill and
needs native's extra scan and setup work reproduced while the vertex segments shrink. The largest identified block

greater-than-zero tests and forcing `xor ebx,ebx` before `push edi`, where native tests registers directly and homes

zero CSE is the only lever found for the offset-11 gate and it is an allocator choice rather than a source one. The
recommended next step is the one hundred and one native-longer bytes between fill1 and fill3, meaning the region
scan, the material-store block, the frees and the region setup, since reproducing that missing work is a

permutation: the object stores `mov [esp+0x10],ebp` at 0x001c against native's `mov [esp+0x34],ebx` at 0x0020, with
initialisation slots object D0, D24, D20 and D8 against native D24, D1c, D20 and Dc, so num at D24 and hits at D20
agree while pc and cnt2 are permuted, which is also why the clamp temporary landed in the object's D0 instead of
native's flag slot D4. The first divergence past the slot colouring is the fv comparison: the object emits
`test ah,0x5; jp` after a `fstp` spill at 0x07fe where native emits `and eax,0x4100; jne` after `fst` and
`fcompp` at 0x086b, because the object spills fv before the gm_RandomFloat01 call while native keeps it on the x87
stack and orders the call before the `fv - num*0x665ed0` step, a genuine evaluation-order difference at
`if (fv > gm_RandomFloat01())`. Scratch probes in .scratch/569ff0/ with probe.sh, nextdiv.py, V1.c, V2.c, V3.c and

## 2026-11-03 — read-only data rows must come from the stub generator

The 46 rows whose reference VAs lie in `.rdata` while their owners emit into `.data` cannot be fixed by editing
their definitions: every owner lives in stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c, whose header states it is auto-generated by
`rebrew build symbol-stubs` and must not be edited by hand, so a manual const qualifier there would be overwritten on
the next regeneration. The decision is therefore to treat it as an upstream generator gap: `rebrew build
symbol-stubs` should emit a `const` definition for a global whose native reference section is `.rdata`, or whose
managed declaration is const-qualified, while leaving `.data` and `.bss` rows and any written symbol alone. The fix
is being made in the upstream checkout at /home/maci/Desktop/Projects/relumea/repos/rebrew with a regression test
that shows a `.rdata` row producing a non-const stub before the change and a const one after, followed by
regenerating the scaffold in this project and re-measuring `.rdata` placement. No scaffold or generated file was
edited by hand for this step.

## 2026-11-03 — production message float compare block parked

`0x569FF0` stays at 982 of 3772 with the object exact and lint clean; the evaluation-order pass kept no edit and the
source is byte-identical to the 982 baseline. Native's target block at 0x56a84e is
call gm_RandomFloat01; fld [esp+0x10]; fld [esp+0x20]; fmul qword [0x665ed0]; fsubp st(1); fst [esp+0x10];
fcompp; fnstsw ax; and eax,0x4100; jne; mov [esp+0x14],1; jmp; mov [esp+0x14],0, which is 58 bytes, while the
baseline at 0x82a does fld; fld; fmul; fsubp; fstp; call; fcomp; then test ah,0x5; jnp for 56 bytes. Four findings
explain why source cannot bridge them. A plain store cannot emit the non-popping `fst`, because fv is dead after the
comparison, so the compiler fuses `fv = fv - prod` into the compare and drops the store; only a volatile store, or a
store to a slot that stays live, forces it. The `jne` polarity is reachable only through the negated condition
`!(fv > rnd)`, since the forward condition emits `je` with a hoisted store. The `mov 1; jmp; mov 0` body is not
produced by this compiler for a two-simple-store if-else, which always merges into one hoisted store plus one
conditional store, so native's block is two bytes longer than ours and the case-5 tail sits 36 bytes ahead of native,
meaning exact sequence content cannot add matches and only a two-byte length delta could shift downstream. And the
same source under msvc-6.0-sp5 without the processor pack gives 724 at object 3788, so the `and eax,0x4100` forms are
not a wrong-profile artifact and the processor-pack profile stays correct. The only probe that reproduced call before
subtraction plus `fst`, `fcompp`, `and eax,0x4100` and `jne` in order at object 3772 was match-neutral and needed a
fabricated volatile qualifier, so it was rejected under the restore rule. A blocker is set on the row. Probes and
results in .scratch/569ff0/ including varA, varF, pr_p, sw_, wv_w1_0, s2, y1 to y3, z2, z3, t_A, t_s2, t_w1,
t_plain and t_final_r3.

stay writable; writes reachable only through `&symbol` or a callee argument are invisible to the source scan and are
documented as such. A mypy failure in the new section-selection code was repaired before the commit by giving the
section variable an explicit optional type and keeping the stored row section in a separate local. Tests cover an
`.rdata` row emitting const, an unchanged `.data` row, pointer constness placement, a const array initialiser, a

## 2026-11-03 — terrain object SIB base rule closes twenty-five bytes

`0x447110` rises from 3319 to 3339 of 3348 with the object still exactly 3348, 114 relocations and status
NEAR_MATCHING; nine byte differences remain and lint is clean. The root cause of the SIB swaph was found and it is a
rule: MSVC 6 keeps the loaded pointer as the SIB base when the address uses a byte-offset accumulator such as
`lights + off + disp`, but keeps the materialised multiply register as base when the byte offset is written as
`index * stride` inside the address, which is why the RD_LIGHT_NINE copies already matched and the byte-offset
accumulator loops did not. Four loops were rewritten to the multiply form with identical address sequences: the two
lights loops use `RD_LIGHTS(object) + off * 0x38 + disp` with `off++` instead of `off += 0x38`, the light-fill loop
iterates `for (i = 0; i < 7; i++)` indexing `RD_LIGHTS(object) + i * 0x38 + disp` in place of
`for (off = 0; off < 0x188; off += 0x38)`, and the resource loop iterates `for (off = 0; off < 3; off++)` indexing
`RD_DRAW(object) + off * 0x4a4 + ...` in place of `for (off = 0; off < 0xdec; off += 0x4a4)`; iteration counts and
strides are unchanged and `off` is dead after each loop, so no value dependence changed. Twenty-five offsets closed:
1656, 1673, 1690, 1707, 1739, 1773, 1790, 2199, 2216, 2233 and 2250 for `lea` SIB swaps, 2489, 2505, 2521, 2545, 2558,
2570, 2583, 2596, 2612, 2628 and 2644 for light-fill store SIB swaps, 2762 for an inline strcpy SIB that closed as a
side effect, and 3182 and 3189 for resource-loop SIB swaps. The nine still open are pure instruction order: at 2186 and
2190 the stores `mov [esp+0x1c],esi` and `mov [esp+0x18],esi`, which are `left = count` and `start = count`, are
emitted in the opposite order to the reference, which writes left then start, and at 1638 to 1642, 1643 and 1647 the
first light loop schedules the induction variable `xor edi,edi` after our `start = count` store rather than before the
two stores. Source permutations that all produced identical bytes: swapping the assignments, a comma statement,
chained `start = left = count`, `start = left`, declaration-order swap, a for-init comma list, pointer and integer
domain casts, `(char*)off + disp`, array subscript, a named offset local and an unsigned counter. Reverting the first
lights loop to the byte-offset form would trade its seven SIB fixes for the five ordering bytes, so the multiply form is
the net win at nine rather than eleven. Sources in .scratch/rd_object/ with base.c as the pre-change state and expF.c as
the current one.

`0x5BA910` is not stub level, contrary to the earlier todo description: the body is a full transcription of 3413 native
instructions with 223 direct call sites and 92 distinct callees, every one of which has a project symbol, and the
blocker is whole-body register allocation rather than coverage. This pass kept edits that raise structural agreement
from 0.9883 to 0.9933 and mnemonic agreement from 0.6973 to 0.7024 while cutting the missing tail from eleven
instructions to one, and the byte match fell from 758 to 732 with the object from 12169 to 12137 against native 11948.
The trade is deliberate: byte agreement here is a longest-common-subsequence count over 3413 instructions that swings
by about thirty bytes per small scheduling change, so a faithful edit can lower it while fidelity improves. Four changes
landed. The status-message chain at 0x5baec2..0x5baf72 was rewritten from a jump-table switch to the native else-if
ladder over the `al` byte with the message ids 0x72f, 0x70f, 0x713, 0x717, 0x71b, 0x737 and default 0x70b in ecx, which
mirrors the native cmp al and je order and removes the ten trailing jump-table instructions. The same site carried a
real semantic bug: the third argument of fcn_00533dc0 was inverted, since native sets 0x73f when the flag is set and
0x741 when it is clear at 0x5baf49..0x5baf65, and the source had them the other way round. The entity loop compare at
0x5baabf became a zero-extending `*(unsigned short*)0x7746cc`, matching `xor ecx,ecx; mov cx,[edx]` rather than a
sign-extending load. The slot clear at 0x5bac98 was verified against the listing, three zero stores and four minus-one
stores followed by a three-iteration paired loop writing -1, and its in-iteration store order was left as the
better-encoding variant because reordering to native order cost 28 bytes of agreement. Two callees the body already
called were declared: `void fcn_0050de80(int, int*)` and `int fcn_005373e0(int, int)`, and a duplicate fcn_0046f740
prototype was removed. Unresolved call bindings remain for __chkstk, fcn_00466330, fcn_00472380, fcn_00502850,
fcn_0051af00, fcn_005462a0 and fcn_0064d41a, with another six outside the extent only because the object is 189 bytes
longer than native.
The first divergence is the saved-register sequence at byte 11. Native pushes ebx, ebp and esi, moves arg1 to esi,
zeroes ebp for the zero register, sets edi to minus one and uses ebx as the loop counter; this build pushes ebx, loads
arg2 into edx, pushes ebp, esi and edi, zeroes ebx, puts arg1 in edi and minus one in ebp, which is the same four roles
rotated by four cycles, and native holds 0x10 in ebx at 0x5bac9f where ours holds zero. Because the colouring depends
on per-pseudo benefit across the whole body, the next step is a matching pass on loop shape in 0x5bb419..0x5bbdd5 and
0x5bc240..0x5bcab6 rather than more transcription, and a continuation is doing that.

## 2026-11-03 — remaining pad audit: spans duplicate emitted bytes

The 128 remaining `_dpad_*` definitions were audited read only, with the full table at .scratch/dpad-audit/report.md.
The guarded relink map has 131 COMMON `_dpad_` symbols: 128 match a current source definition and their sizes sum to
16,823,361 exactly, while three (100f8c0, 99ef80, 99ec10) have no current source definition and are excluded. The
reference `.data` spans 0x675000 to 0x157e424 for VirtualSize 0xf09424, but its raw bytes end at 0x6b6000, so everything
from 0x6b6000 to 0x157e424, 15,500,324 bytes, is zero-fill virtual space. Every one of the 128 pads has its entire
encoded range inside that tail: none starts before 0x6b6000, the last ends exactly at 0x157e424, and none is
raw-backed, so no pad is out of section. Their encoded union is 14,833,349 bytes, 666,975 short of the tail, and they
duplicate each other by 1,990,012 bytes.
The root cause of the remaining 7,541,760-byte excess is that the pads are COMMON: they never sit at their encoded VAs
but are appended after the real objects, which already emit 6,450,496 bytes of `.data` and `.bss`, so the same reference
bytes are modelled twice. The defect is therefore not a wrong pad VA but a pad span over bytes that are already
emitted. Grouping the 128 pads: 13 are fully redundant for 1,990,600 bytes, 115 are partly redundant for 14,832,761
bytes of which 3,147,018 bytes are proven redundant while the remainder stands for reference zero fill nothing else
emits, and none is needed with no proven overlap. Proven redundancy totals 5,137,618 bytes against the measured excess
of 7,541,760, and 2,404,142 bytes cannot be attributed per pad because 3,982 defined globals have no reference VA and
the scaffold source is smaller than the linked symbol_stubs.c.obj. A robust lower bound independent of object sizes is
the pad-to-pad duplication of 1,990,012 bytes plus 1,125,492 bytes of overrun past the next modelled row, which is
3,115,504.
Six pads overrun the next modelled row, for 1,125,492 bytes: _dpad_6b89e4 from 760,604 to 4, _dpad_fb5740 from 327,904
to 32, _dpad_9b0e20 from 36,896 to 16, _dpad_14ce8c2 from 94 to 30, _dpad_773de8 from 2,200 to 2,156 and _dpad_6b870c
from 728 to 696. The documented rule from the data-analysis skill and the ownership documents is that a pad is
warranted only for proven uncovered storage or alignment, and a pad over bytes already emitted is not, with the further
guidance that reference fillers must not be recreated. The recommended order is to trim the six overruns first, then
delete the eleven pads that are still fully covered after the trims, because deleting all thirteen at once is not
consistent: trimming _dpad_6b89e4 releases _dpad_6f2578, _dpad_770ae8 and _dpad_6b870c from containment, so the joint
set is eleven drops. The combined effect is 2,469,688 bytes removed and `.data` VirtualSize from 23,308,324 to
20,838,636, leaving 5,072,072 of excess concentrated in _dpad_aed32c at 5,014,548 bytes and _dpad_1052c50 at
4,498,744 bytes, which must be split around the named objects inside them rather than deleted. A caveat from the
2026-10-29 entry is carried forward: shrinking oversized pads once dropped same-offset agreement from 249,682 to
239,806 and removing pads dropped the match, so any change here needs a relink comparison, and a pad another target
needs should be guarded with the existing
`#if defined(REBREW_SERVER) || defined(REBREW_GOLD)` form rather than deleted.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: scattered constant stores reproduced

`0x4DA690` rises from 882 to 1340 matching bytes (19.0 percent) with 72 relocations, status SIZE_MISMATCH and lint
clean, and the object is 7048 against native 7057, having been exact before the pass, while the first divergence moves
from offset 155 to 158. The root cause fixed was the six `blkB.order[]` constant stores: native scatters them into the
string-copy fill stalls of the sitzung table, one after the `rep stosd` of sitzung[1] and five after sitzung[4]'s, at
target offsets 155 and 392 to 436, whereas this build emitted them as one contiguous statement block after the local
initialisers, which displaced every byte after offset 155. Declaring the values as an initialised array as the first
local, before the string tables, reproduces the scatter exactly, and target offsets 155 to 838 now match apart from
single-byte differences: the six store displacements at 158, 395, 406, 417, 428 and 439 and a few register-allocation
bytes at 544, 565, 703, 765, 781, 797, 805, 814, 820, 824 and 834. The remaining first divergence at offset 158 is the
store displacement, native `mov dword [esp+0xb8],6` against `[esp+0xa8]`, because the separate order array lands
0x10 low.
Three walls were measured and not chased. Five declaration shapes failed to move the order array from 0xa8 to native's
0xb8; moving `s98[4]` before the order array collapses the frame from 0x900 to 0x8f0 and drops the match to 704, and
putting the array back inside the aggregate kills the scatter and drops it to 882 at object 1280. `rebrew diagnose
stack` reports a target frame of 0x980 against a compiled 0x924 while the esp-relative slots agree at sitzung 0x1e4,
sD0 0xd0 and sF4 0x104. From about offset 0x30e native keeps `a0` in ebx and the zero in ebp where this build has them
swapped, which costs the nine-byte size shortfall. The body from target offset 1058 onward is still approximate: loop
shapes, `s44` kept in memory where native keeps it in a register, `order[s20]` constant-folded to 6 where native loads
the slot at 0xc0, and the sel and s98 bases at 0xa8 against native's 0xc0, which is what keeps the row at STUB.
Unresolved callees with null bound addresses: _fcn_004727a0 with 24 references, _fcn_0064d41a with 6, _fcn_0051af00
with 2 and _fcn_004e4eb0 with 1.

## 2026-11-03 — terrain object nine byte ordering wall

`0x447110` stays at 3339 of 3348 with object 3348, 114 relocations and status NEAR_MATCHING; the pair-ordering pass kept
no edit and the source is byte-identical to the session start. Both remaining regions are pure instruction
permutations with no encoding difference. At 1638 the reference emits `xor edi,edi; mov [esp+0x1c],esi` for
`left = count` and then `mov [esp+0x18],esi` for `start = count`, while this build emits `mov [esp+0x18],esi;
xor edi,edi; mov [esp+0x1c],esi`, and at 2183 the reference writes left then start where this build swaps them. The
reference order equals the source statement order, and 19 compiles were byte-identical at nine differences: statement
swap, full reverse, `start = left`, a temporary local, an unfoldable expression between the stores, a pointer store
through `*(int*)(void*)&start`, a comma statement, a for-init comma list, declaration swap, combined declaration,
renaming, a long form, an unsigned form with a cast on the guard, a nested block, `do { } while (0)`, and a folded if,
each applied to the first loop only, the second loop only and both. Order is not globally forced, since the pair at
offsets 31 and 35 keeps descending source order in both images, and only this count-valued pair reorders. As a
diagnostic, deleting `start = count` from the first loop changed the size to 3324 and swapped the slot assignment with
start at 0x1c and left at 0x18 while the emitted order stayed start then left, so the earlier apparent flip was slot
renaming rather than an ordering change. With start fixed at 0x18, left at 0x1c and both stores sourced from esi, the
required order is not reachable from C within the allowed edit scope, and closing only the pair would leave the
`xor edi,edi` placement wrong, so it would not have been a kept improvement. A blocker is set on the row. Variant
matrix and details in .scratch/rd_object/NOTES-row-00447110.md.

## 2026-11-03 — largest row: colouring pass finds the loops already clean

`0x5BA910` rises from 732 to 750 matching bytes with the object at 12136 from 12137, against native 11948, status
SIZE_MISMATCH with 44 relocations and lint clean. One change was kept and four reverted. The kept change makes the
fill-loop calls pass the `a1` parameter instead of `f.v14` at lines 607 and 608, matching native's load of
`[esp+0x1864]` at 0x5bb463; that is worth 18 matched bytes and one object byte, and the same substitution in the release
loop at lines 561 to 565 lost 45 matched bytes and added six object bytes because the zero constant occupies the natural
register there, so it was reverted. The other reverted probes: adding the missing pointer dereference at the seven-loop
compare, which is native-correct but cost 31 matched bytes and two object bytes with no structural gain; splitting the
assignment from the call, which was byte-identical; writing the global as an indexed array, which was byte-identical; and
the release-loop substitution above. The saved-register sequence did not move under any probe and still emits
push ebx, `mov 0x1854(%esp),%edx`, push ebp, push esi, push edi and `xor ebx,ebx`, with arg1 in edi, the zero in ebx and
minus one in ebp, where native pushes ebx, ebp and esi, moves arg1 to esi, pushes edi, zeroes ebp and sets edi to minus
one.
Three findings reset the plan. Both named loop regions already match native in shape, so loop-shape edits have no defect
to fix: the entity and empty-slot scans at 0x5bb419..0x5bbdd5 are instruction-for-instruction identical with only the
counter register differing, and the outer slot walk with its inner three-slot loop at 0x5bc240..0x5bcab6 reloads and
decrements exactly as native does, so the divergence is colouring alone. The body spills more than native, with 771
against 718 stack memory operands and 139 against 119 large-displacement forms, which accounts for the 188-byte excess
better than any instruction shape and makes the size gap and the rotation the same symptom. And the first structural
cause of the rotation is the seven-iteration packet loop at native 0x5baa9f, where this build materialises
`0x14a56e8 - &f.vD4[0]` in a register with `mov $0x14a56e8,%ebp; lea 0xe0(%esp),%edx; sub %edx,%ebp;
mov (%esi,%ebp,1),%eax`, clobbering the minus-one register and forcing a second minus-one range at object 0x210, where
native uses `[esi+0x14a56e8]` with esi as `i*4` and keeps a single minus-one range from 0x5ba945 to 0x5bafc2; three
source variants on that loop produce byte-identical code, so the pointer base is the allocator's choice. The
recommendation is to stop treating the loop regions as the lever and work the 53 extra frame accesses instead, whose
first fixable case is making the seven-loop use native's index form. Backups in .scratch/5ba910/ with g_p1.c as the kept
state, base.c as the baseline and g_LEDGER.md as the probe ledger. A transient CatalogScanError from `rebrew diff`
against another session's d2 file recovered without intervention and did not affect any number above.

## 2026-11-03 — io_AppendText copy forms and a wrong extent

`0x519190` rises from 681 to 684 matching bytes and its extent is corrected from 7536 to 7527, so the object now equals
the reference extent exactly at 7527 with 79 relocations and lint clean; status is STUB because 684 of 7527 is below
the sixty percent threshold. Two edits landed. The case 'f' join copy became `memmove` instead of `memcpy`, matching
native's call to 0x64d740, where the object had inlined a `rep movs`; that is worth three matched bytes. And the local
prototype of fcn_00517c00 took an `unsigned char` second argument, matching the owning definition in
src/Develop/Unassigned/GOLDTL.fcn_00517c00.c and the listing, which clears the C4047 and C4024 diagnostics without
changing bytes. Reverted with measurements: the else-branch copy plus length became `strcpy` for 588 at object 7515; a
global `memcpy` to `memmove` sweep cost the local equality case and gave 761 from 807; recomputing the carry-block value
gave 700; replacing the fail label and goto with `return -1` gave 753; a manual digit loop for case 'r' gave 735; case
'S' as `memmove` gave 710; and five declaration-order permutations produced byte-identical objects.
The extent repair is evidenced directly: the function's code ends at 0x51aef6 and nine 0x90 bytes fill 0x51aef7 to
0x51aeff before the next row at 0x51af00, so the true extent is 0x1D67 or 7527. The earlier nine-byte size difference
was that padding, and the object's own section is already 0x1d70 with identical padding, so the recorded extent could
never be reached from C. The repair ran through `rebrew binary repair-extents 0x519190=7527 --sync-rows` with preview
digest 81abfa4fb7116091bb5a6da4e73878f48467184d47c6e1735534c622d70b85ae.
Walls confirmed and recorded: the frame immediate is unreachable because a `work[]` sweep from 0x17c8 to 0x17d0 yields
only 0x31f0 or 0x31f8, since the eight-byte-aligned aggregate rounds to eight while the text buffer stays at esp+0x260;
`/O2` always merges this function's minus-one returns into one epilogue, so native's four inline guard epilogues and one
fail block cannot be reproduced from C, and the earlier blocker text claiming `and esp,-8` is never emitted is stale
because the first seven bytes do match; and the stack and register layout differ with native's ap at 0x10, v14 at 0x20,
v10 at 0x1c, v1c at 0x28, v30 at 0x38 and v2c at 0x3c against this build's ap at 0x18, v14 at 0x2c, v10 at 0x24, v1c at
0x30, v30 at 0x3c and v2c at 0x38, while the buffers agree at text 0x260, work 0x1a30, abuf 0xa0 and rbuf 0x80, which
makes the slots liveness-driven rather than declaration-order driven. The switch index table at 0x1d14 to 0x1d67 is
byte-identical with all 26 index-to-case mappings matching, and the case layout follows source order except that the
optimizer places case 'F' after 'm'. Unresolved callees without project definitions: fcn_0064d530, fcn_0064d740,
fcn_0064d41a, fcn_00657a73 and fcn_0064eeec, plus the CRT toupper, isdigit and string helpers, and fcn_004fe330 has only
a GOLD definition. One tool defect was found: `rebrew diagnose gap 0x00519190 --json` crashes with a TypeError about a
bytearray used as a dict key at rebrew/gap_trace.py:143, and that failure belongs upstream.

## 2026-11-03 — forty six more pads split, with the alignment rule

The remaining partially redundant pads were split in three measured batches, taking `.data` VirtualSize from 19,233,092
to 17,902,244 for a drop of 1,330,848 and leaving an excess of 2,135,680 over the reference 15,766,564. A new fact gated
the method: COMMON contributions are thirty-two-byte aligned, which the giant split proved because its fifteen pieces
sum to 7,907,840 under align32 and that is exactly what was allocated. A split therefore only shrinks `.data` when
align32 of the original size exceeds the sum of align32 of the pieces, and of 113 pads with named coverage only 48 had a
positive delta, the other 65 having gaps of one to a hundred bytes where each piece costs thirty-two. Only the 48 were
edited, in three batches with measurements: batch 1 changed 3 pads in 3 files for a predicted 1,301,664 and a measured
1,301,696; batch 2 changed 17 pads in 14 files for a predicted 27,040 and measured 27,296; batch 3 changed 28 pads in 24
files for a predicted 1,664 and measured 2,080; and two pads in one file were reverted for 224 bytes, giving 46 pads
across 37 files, a predicted 1,330,144 and a measured 1,330,848. The 46 originals became 186 pieces, each original stays
inside the `#if defined(REBREW_SERVER) || defined(REBREW_GOLD)` guard and the client branch holds only gap pieces, and a
checker asserts for all 37 files and 46 pads that the pieces equal the computed gaps, that the guard keeps the original
size, and that pieces plus named objects equal the span.

19,233,092 to 17,902,244, `.data1` moves from 0x18da000 to 0x1795000 and `.rsrc` from 0x18db000 to 0x1796000, with map
symbols from 15,778 to 15,918 and section-3 rows from 6,094 to 6,234. The 512-byte `.text` drop is not from the pads:
rebuilding src/Develop/Units/d2.v1/GOLDTL.fcn_004d6170.c, which holds `_dpad_772d14`, showed that the stale
build-goldtl-audit object predates a committed change, since the current source compiles to 4,928 bytes of `.text` where

## 2026-11-03 — upstream gap trace crash fixed

The `rebrew diagnose gap` crash found while working `0x519190` is fixed upstream in commit bf6a0bbe on the main branch of
the checkout at /home/maci/Desktop/Projects/relumea/repos/rebrew, not pushed. The traceback reproduced from this project
is `TypeError: cannot use 'bytearray' as a dict key (unhashable type: 'bytearray')` raised inside
difflib.SequenceMatcher's chain_b when `trace_gaps` builds the matcher at gap_trace.py:143. The cause is that capstone
exposes `insn.bytes` as a bytearray and the masked-key branch computed `raw[:1] + b"\x00" * (...)`; slicing a bytearray
yields a bytearray, and difflib uses those masked keys as dictionary keys. The fix makes `_masked_key` return
`bytes(raw[:1]) + ...` on that branch so every path returns bytes, and a review found no other dictionary key in the file
that could receive a bytearray, since `first_fault` and `_obj_text` key by integer and `_seq` uses the masked key tuple.
The regression test `tests/test_new_commands.py::TestGapTraceHelpers::test_diagnose_gap_keeps_bytearray_stream_hashable`
drives `diagnose gap f.c --va 0x1000 --json` through `rebrew.app.main` with compile and disassembly patched so both sides
carry an equal byte run, asserts exit zero and a structured payload with va, instruction counts and a null fault, and it
was confirmed to fail before the fix with the same TypeError. Verification: the exact failing command now exits zero and
prints JSON through the checkout CLI, the suite reports 13,730 passed with 29 skipped, ruff passes and mypy reports no
issues across 413 files, with pre-commit hooks passing on the commit. One caveat is recorded: the PATH executable at
/home/maci/.local/bin/rebrew is a uv tool install of release 6.16.0 and still carries the crash, and it was deliberately
not reinstalled, since the project uses its pinned environment rather than an editable checkout.

## 2026-11-03 — largest row parked on the colouring wall

`0x5BA910` keeps 750 at object 12136 with 771 stack operands against native's 718 and a saved-register sequence of
push ebx, arg1 into edx, push ebp, push esi, push edi and `xor ebx,ebx`, where native holds arg1 in esi, the zero in ebp
and minus one in edi. Five probes this pass all regressed and were reverted. Using the slot offset as a new local in both
three-slot loops took stack operands from 771 to 761 and big displacements to 121 but dropped the match to 735 at object
12178, because the frame grew from 0x1848 to 0x184c and every displacement shifted by four. Reusing dead locals instead
of declaring one gave an identical result, so the growth comes from extra cross-call liveness rather than the
declaration. The seven-loop byte-offset index kept stack operands at 771 and dropped the match to 717 at object 12200,
since MSVC then materialises two derived pointers. Folding `h` into the index was byte-identical, so `h` already shares a
slot. Dropping the `i` temporary in the slot loop raised stack operands to 779 and dropped the match to 733 at object
12255.
Three findings redirect the plan. The frame is exactly at native size 0x1848 with zero slack, so any value live across a
call costs a four-byte slot, and that shift is worth more than the ten stack operands it buys; introducing a local to
keep a value in a register cannot work on this function as modelled. The seven-loop is worth only about two of the 53
excess stack operands, because the excess is diffuse: 103 call-anchored windows differ and 80 of them have matching
instruction counts at plus one to plus four, so even a perfect seven-loop fix cannot move the 53. And a real defect was
found: the source uses `f.v9c` as a per-slot scratch at lines 1111 and 1383, while native never stores those values,
keeping the per-slot offset in esi across ten calls at 0x5bc8ce..0x5bcbf1, with slot 0x9c holding only the scaled offset
from line 484 that lines 1442 and 1446 read, so the loop writes also clobber that value. The fix is directionally right at
ten stack operands but blocked on freeing a callee-saved register. Address taking is not the lever either: `lea` with esp
is 64 in native against 69 here. The recommendation is to stop source-shape probes on this row until a register can be
freed. A blocker records all of this, including the unfixed `f.v9c` defect. Instruments in .scratch/5ba910/ with
s_probe.py, s_stack.py, s_align.py, s_region.py and s_pull.py.

## 2026-11-03 — identity rows for globals that had no reference address

A read-only derivation pass established which globals can be given a reference address from evidence and which cannot.
Inventory: 4,344 globals were scanned and 432 row names found, so 3,912 have no row, of which 3,775 are source-defined
and 137 declaration-only; the 3,775 split into 545 pad, lead and gap names whose VA is in the name, 3,202 scaffold stub
definitions and 28 real source definitions, with the stubs encoding 2,794 `.data` or `.bss` addresses, 268 `.rdata`
addresses, 6 `.text` addresses and 134 without a hex value. The audit's earlier figure of 3,982 is 4,344 minus the 362
globals whose name matches a row, so it counted declaration-only rows and treated names as having no VA.
The evidence route was tested rather than assumed. Anchors are the 3,233 map symbols with a known reference VA, 415 rows
and 2,818 name-encoded, and their emitted order disagrees with reference order in only 34 of 3,232 consecutive pairs, or
1.05 percent, but only 4 anchor runs have equal built and reference spans, which fixes just 6 interior symbols, while
2,639 interior symbols sit in unequal spans. Emitted order plus boundary VAs is therefore not sufficient, and the
structural reason is that pad piece starts were themselves computed as previous reference VA plus built extent, so pad
spans re-encode the same built extents and add no independent bound. What does work is the name encoding corroborated by
an exact fit, where the next encoded VA minus this VA equals the emitted extent: 936 objects pass, 738 `.bss` and 198 raw
`.data`, of which 197 raw `.data` ones are unique and collision-free and 155 have nonzero reference bytes that decode
consistently with the declared type. The ambiguous remainder is 1,865 encoded without an exact fit, 32 overlapping the
next anchor, 42 sharing a reference VA, 408 stubs without a `.data` hex, 28 real definitions and 23 absent from the map.
The convention applied follows docs/data-ownership.md line 39, which allows an unsized identity-only GLOBAL row to
record an address without asserting ownership, so rows carry `--kind GLOBAL`, name, size only where the exact fit proves
it, section and file, with no storage kind, backing or link symbol, and placeholder names stay. The first batch of 20 rows
was previewed with digest 2e9595fe7bf7b5e03f75055c4ab6849eddece9dd6280c14b03e3f48a64c117d6 and applied through
`rebrew data set --expected-digest`: 0x675308 as float 1.0f, 0x67530c, 0x675310 and 0x675314 as int -1, 0x67531c as
int 1, 0x675320 and 0x675324 as int 256, 0x677188 through 0x6771a0 as int -1 to -7, 0x678150 as float 1.0f, 0x678154 and
0x678158 as float -1.0f, 0x67815c as unsigned 5000 and 0x67a28c and 0x67a290 as float -1.0f. Lint passes after the write
with no errors and no new size, overlap or stale-evidence warnings. Two caveats are recorded: address rows do not move
`.data` VirtualSize, since only extents do, and only the 936 exact-fit objects have extent evidence; and these rows are
placeholder-owned, so `rebrew verify --data` must not be run against them because the built bytes are zeros while the
reference bytes are real, and they must never be given a storage kind of object.

proves declaration order does not affect slot assignment; declarator initialisers give 0x764 and raw 951; and fsum before
didFolter gives 0x764 and raw 919. The reason is that every variant producing the two head zero stores extends the fsum
and didFolter live ranges to the function top, and with the p38 spill already occupying the twelfth slot the frame grows
by four bytes, with `sub esp,0x764` and msg at 0x44 and rec at 0x244, so divergence moves to offset 0x02 instead of past
0x18. Removing xpad costs 623 matched bytes, so it is load-bearing. The recommendation is that the blocker is register
allocation rather than declarations: recover what native keeps in ebx, esi and ebp and why this compile spills p38, likely
one extra simultaneously live scalar, and once the spill disappears the two head initialisations fit without growing the
frame. Evidence and the variant table are in .scratch/004dcf50-findings.md with helpers in
.scratch/goldtl-004dcf50-tools/.

per-row scene pass from 0x757 to 0x1165 is 2574 against 2577 for plus 3, the second packet pass from 0x1165 to 0x1b09 is
2468 against 2509 for plus 41, and the epilogue from 0x1b09 to 0x1b91 is 136 against 91 for minus 45, giving minus 37 in
total. So the per-row pass is three bytes over rather than short, and the call sequences are identical on both sides at 223
calls in one-to-one correspondence, which means no native block and no callee is missing; the deficit is the pre-pass
region at minus 33, the second pass at plus 41 and the tail at minus 45, the last being the fourteen-argument escape block
native does not have.
The prefix stops at 0x31f because of scalar frame slots: the first mismatch is the displacement of native's

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: slots are not addressable and the loop shape was misread

`0x4DA690` keeps 1489 at object 7020 with prefix 0x31f and an unchanged source; three findings change the plan for this
row. First, slot layout is not addressable and therefore cannot be iterated: probes in .scratch/4da690/r14 where one int
declaration list is reversed, where eight separate int statements are reversed, and where the same declarations keep their
order but the assignment order swaps show the first two compile to byte-identical text while only the assignment-order
change differs, so stack slots follow the generated body alone. Reordering all sixty declarations is the same negative and
adding locals moves the frame instead, with two addressed ints taking the prefix to 0x2, so "iterate the scalar set with
the frame held at 0x900" has no lever: a slot moves only when the whole function's liveness moves. Second, the count
handling was already native: keeping the count in s44 and dropping `k` produces an object byte-identical to the baseline,
and native storing the count to one slot twice at 0x348 and 0x375 matches the object storing at 0x348 and 0x378, so the
earlier claim of a second slot is not in the object and the item is closed. Third, the row's loop shape is already native's
and the e4 variant is the wrong shape: native's per-row back edge is `jl 0x4dae03`, offset 0x773, which is the s1C load
and test, while 0x77f is the body entry rather than a branch target, and the object back-edges to its own s1C load and test
at 0x788. Both test s1C on every row, so `if (s1C == 0) break;` at the top of the do loop is correct and the e4 hoist
contradicts native; e4 also costs 92 matched bytes and improves the slot-blind body score only from 1314 to 1317 aligned
instructions, so it was reverted.
Sizes bracket the target without prefix growth: the baseline is 7020, e4 is 7065 and a variant that recomputes `s00` at the
head without the incremental add is 7049, with native 7057 between the last two; all failed the keep rule and were
reverted, with that variant kept at .scratch/4da690/r14/c3_loop_recompute_s00.c. The slot-blind score shows where the body
really differs: 1975 native instructions against 1972 in the object with shape similarity 0.666 and 1314 aligned, and all
large gaps sit in the second packet pass, where native 0x170a to 0x1892 of 113 instructions has 1 in the object, the
object's 0x15c7 to 0x17bd of 138 has none in native, native 0x1668 to 0x16fc of 40 is missing, the object's 0x148c to
0x1595 of 70 is extra and native 0x1995 to 0x1a50 of 51 has 1. That region therefore does not merely run 41 bytes over;
it holds two relocated blocks of roughly 110 instructions, and the epilogue figure is polluted by the escape block at
object 0x1b01 to 0x1b63 which native has nowhere. The next round should drive the body to native shape and stop chasing
slots, since the prefix only moves once the allocator sees a near-native body, and should use the slot-blind score as its
metric rather than the prefix. Tools added: fslots.py to list every reference to one folded frame slot, slotmap.py to learn
the object-to-native slot map from a shape-blind alignment, and score.py to print the slot-blind body score with its
mismatched regions.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: the block relocation premise is an alignment artifact

`0x4DA690` keeps 1489 at object 7020 with frame 0x900 and an unchanged source, and the score to beat is a mismatch of
1329 giving shape 0.663 with 1309 aligned instructions out of 1975 native and 1972 object instructions. The previous
round's region list reproduces exactly only when general-purpose registers are folded before diffing, which yields native
0x170a with 113 instructions against the object's 0x18f1 with 1, a deleted native block at 0x1668 of 40 instructions, an
inserted object block at 0x15c7 of 138 and a native 0x1995 block of 51; with the score canonicalisation that is
register-sensitive, the same code aligns as many small opcodes. A content check settles it: the candidate's second-pass
scan `push #12de` sits at 0x168e against native's 0x171b, a delta of 0x8d, and the apparently missing native 0x1668 to
0x16fc block is the candidate's 0x15c7 to 0x1644 block, with `push eax`, call, `push #3e8`, and `cmp eax,#-1`
identically shaped. Mnemonic-only alignment gives shape 0.875 with a single gap, the known object-only escape block at
0x1b01 to 0x1b62 of 35 instructions, so no statements are relocated or missing and there is only drift.
The real cause is push-depth drift. The score folds slots relative to minus four times the push depth, and the depth
diverges at the vote and packet pass and never returns: an aligned block at native 0x00e8c has depth 14 against the
object's 4, and by the count-is-zero and count-greater-than-one bodies it is 29 against 16, a delta of 13. From that point
every scaled slot token differs, which is exactly what appeared as the 138-instruction insert and 113-instruction delete.
Native also keeps roughly 0x140 bytes more code before the second pass than the object, which supplies the offset shift.
Four experiments were discarded with the source restored and the score unchanged at 1329: the parked
c3_loop_recompute_s00 variant gives 1977 object bytes and 7055 with a mismatch of 1496, worse alignment and closer size;
rewriting the initialisation loop at source lines 211 to 219 as one stepped base with `pb += 0x35c/4` and negative indexed
access to match native's single-base form gives 1984 at 7039 and a mismatch of 1341; declaring sDC as `unsigned char` in
both positions changes object bytes but leaves the score at 1329; and removing the synthetic escape block at source lines
818 to 823 gives 1828 object bytes at 6527 with a mismatch of 1314 and shape 0.654, worse because the denominator shrinks.
Two concrete leads were measured for the next attempt. Native's packet struct at &sD8 is an int at [esp+0xf4], a hole at

local because the compiler drops it. Tools in .scratch/4da690/r15/ with rep.py for merged regions, shift.py for the

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row reaches exact size via the switch form

`0x4DA690` now has object 7057, exactly native, with match 1456, 71 relocations, frame 0x900 and status STUB. The switch
form trades 62 matched bytes for size parity, and the trade is taken deliberately: clearing the size gate is the ladder's
requirement before a row can be matched further, and this row's measured depth anchors improve at the same time, from plus
one and plus one at 0xbbd and 0xbd9 to zero and zero, with the later anchors moving from plus six, plus eight and plus ten
to plus four, plus three and plus five.
The root finding is a compiler rule: this compiler cross-jumps `call` plus `add esp` only, never argument setup, unless the
arm block ends at the differing parameter push. Three probes establish it, with identical call tails still merging only the
call and cleanup, while a hoisted register argument lets it merge `push 0`, `push reg`, the call and the `add`. Native's
six-instruction tail needs `mov ecx,[0x772514]` to be common after the constant push, whereas our arms schedule that load
before the push and into three different registers, so only the call and cleanup can merge.
Measured variants: the baseline is 1518 at object 7071 with window 216 instructions and 64 pushes, aligned 1140, shape
0.577 and mismatch 1266; the switch form is 1456 at object 7057 with 215 and 63, aligned 1110, shape 0.560 and mismatch
1342; a common tail for all three arms is 1435 at 7037 with 217 and 62, aligned 1154, shape 0.585 and mismatch 1229; a
common tail for two arms with the third inline is 1517 at 7060 with 215 and 64, aligned 1158, shape 0.585 and mismatch
1234; and hoisting the load to a local is 1473 at 7056 with 215 and 65, aligned 1021, shape 0.518 and mismatch 1549. The
switch form lays cases out in decreasing value order, default then one then zero, against native's 0, 1, 2, and rewriting
the case source order produces byte-identical output. An `/Os` diagnostic does produce the merged constant-push arm tail
but adds a frame pointer and memory-push arguments, so it is unusable since native is /Ot. The previous state is preserved
at .scratch/4da690/r16/pre_switch_1518.c, and the variants live beside it.

## 2026-11-03 — text formatter: two wrong operands corrected

`0x51C840` rises from 1397 to 1425 matching bytes with object 6043 against native 6048 and 125 relocations, keeping the
jump table at 0x16E8 and the character map at 0x1748 byte-identical. Two listing-verified corrections landed, both of them
wrong operands rather than alignment. In case 'D' at native 0x125f to 0x12dc the source had
`memmove(buf + strlen(tmp), buf + i, strlen(tmp) + 2 - i)` where native has
`memmove(buf + i - 2 + strlen(tmp), buf + i, strlen(buf) + 2 - i)`, with the count built as `len(buf) + 2 - i` through
`mov eax,2; sub eax,ebp; add ecx,eax` and the destination as `lea eax,[ecx+edx-2]` with the length in ecx and buf+i in edx,
so both operands were wrong and not merely unaligned; measured alone it gives object 6047 with the table at 0x16EC and
match 1059. In case 'i' with r not equal to minus one at native 0x87b to 0x8aa the source had
`res = strlen(tmp)/3 + strlen(tmp) - 1` where the listing computes a multiply by 0xaaaaaaab, shifts edx right by one, adds
the length, and forms `lea edi,[esp+esi+0x24]` as num plus res with no decrement; measured alone it gives object 6039 with
the table at 0x16E4 and match 1086. Combined the object is 6043 at table 0x16E8 with match 1425.
The first divergence after the parked prologue is the digit guard at offset 0x192: native spans 25 bytes from 0x186 with
`movsx esi,buf[i+1]; inc ebp; sub esi,0x30; js L; cmp esi,9; jg L; inc ebp; jmp J; L: or esi,-1`, while this build spans 28
with `cmp $0x9,%esi; ja L2; inc ebp; or ecx,-1; jmp J; L2: or ecx,-1; mov esi,ecx`. The body root is minus-one common
subexpression elimination: this build carries eleven two-byte `cmp %ecx,%esi` and sixty-eight `or $0xffffffff,%ecx` where
native has thirteen three-byte `cmp esi,-1` and immediate `mov dword [mem],0xffffffff` at both case 'm' stores, which is
the whole eight-byte case 'm' difference, and the constant is commoned by value rather than spelling, which is why earlier
respellings produced byte-identical objects.
Size cannot be fixed piecemeal: the net size before the table must stay exactly zero or the 0x16E8 table, the 0x1748 map
and the 439, 291, 66, 52 and 33-byte matching runs all move. The per-case extents are +1, +1, -52, -27, -1, +3, +18, -8,
-45, +19, -41, -1, +19, -9, -26, +48, +15 and +86 for S, F, T, w, i, I, m, W, u, b, B, E, N, a, r, D and G, summing to zero.
Correct-but-costly changes were measured and reverted with both numbers: converting case T's strcpy to a length copy gives
object 6059, table 0x16F8 and match 1083; the same in case 'I' with r equal to minus one gives 6071, 0x1704 and 1093;
dropping three unsigned-char casts on the G toupper gives 6027, 0x16D8 and 1090; combining the T fix with the cast fix holds
the table at 0x16E8 with object 6043 but still costs 288 matched bytes because the movsx rewrite collapses a 439-byte run to
a 184-byte table run; and converting case S's initial strcpy to a length copy gives 6023, 0x16D4 and 973. Unresolved callees:
fcn_0064eeec has no row and only a link scaffold stub, with the prototype retained as `int __cdecl fcn_0064eeec(char*)`;
fcn_004fe330 is not unresolved, since it is the cross-target row 0x00500e00 bound at 5246464; every other callee has a row.
Also recorded: the five-byte object shortfall is the native section tail's five padding NOPs after the character map at
0x179B to 0x17A0, which a COFF object never emits, so object 6048 is unreachable from C. The prologue blocker stands
untouched, with native loading [0x6a23a0] before [0x6a239c] and the first mismatched byte at 0x21. Notes in
.scratch/51c840/NOTES_block3.md with the harness at try.py.

## 2026-11-03 — a function reaches full relocation match

`0x535BD0` now measures RELOC with 739 of 739 bytes matching, object 739, zero byte mismatches and 37 relocations, of
which 22 call sites validate and 15 are compiler-generated local labels. Three things had to be corrected and one extent
repaired. The file binding is src/Develop/Unassigned/fcn_00535bd0.c, since the d2 path named in the request does not exist.
The store's extent was 752, and independent confirmation found the code plus its embedded switch tables ending at 0x535eb3
for 739 bytes with thirteen 0x90 fill bytes up to the next 16-aligned function at 0x535ec0, so the extent was repaired to
739 through `rebrew binary repair-extents 0x535bd0=739 --sync-rows` with preview digest bd1c4781; that repair excluded the
fill and is what cleared the size mismatch, since source can never emit it.
The switch dispatch was wrong in both set and mapping. The source had cases 4, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 22, 24, 27, 29 and
30 with a range bound of 0x1a, while native bounds at 0x2a with a 43-entry index table; decoding the jump table at 0x535e54
of 13 dwords and the index bytes at 0x535e88 gives the real cases as 4, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 25, 30, 32, 35, 37 and 46, and
the value-to-block mapping was also wrong, with native value 4 running the 0x6a2c08 toggle rather than the 0x7e2a9c call.
Because MSVC 6 emits switch bodies in source order, the native body order 37, 35, 19, 23, 30, 32, 46, 20, 21, 18, 4, 25 is
the case order. Eight toggle cases were rewritten from `if (x == 0) { x = 1; ... }`, which stores only on the true path, to
`if (*(int*)p = (*(int*)p == 0))`, which computes the boolean, stores it unconditionally and then branches, as native does
with `sete`. Case 20's callee returns a float, since native has `fstp st(0)`, its first argument is a 16-bit load and its
second is -1000, giving the prototype `float __cdecl fcn_004ff210(unsigned short, int)`. Cases 37 and 19 share a single
`char* object_entry` local, without which MSVC copies the pointer and hoists the case-21 buffer push, and that sharing is
load-bearing at 739 bytes against 313 for independent locals. Six callee prototypes were replaced with the project's real
identities, `fcn_00533a40(char*)`, `fcn_005b54b0(char*)`, `fcn_004bfe00(char*)` returning int, `fcn_00502cd0(int, int, ...)`
returning an `unsigned short*`, `fcn_004ff210` and `fcn_004c5790(char, char*)`, which took all 24 call relocations from
unresolved to validating at the right VAs.
There is no remaining body divergence: `rebrew diff` reports target 739 and candidate 739 across 244 instructions with 193
exact and 51 relocation-masked, zero structural, zero register and zero invalid, and `rebrew diagnose stack` shows a
128-byte frame with no frame pointer and no slot differences. The wall is that 15 relocations are compiler-generated local
labels with no store symbol, so masking them is the strongest claim available, and the row is RELOC rather than EXACT.
Flag trials confirmed the row's own flags: `/O2 /Gd /G6` gives 193 at 743 and `/Ox /Gd` gives 313 at 739, so nothing was
promoted. Instruments and measurement table in .scratch/fcn_00535bd0/.

## 2026-11-03 — four extent shrinks reverted, and why

Four inventory extents were shrunk earlier tonight on the strength of a small-row sweep that reported the function bodies
ending before their extents. The shrinks were 0x5efd86 from 4 to 3, 0x65a20a from 29 to 5, 0x64d1df from 73 to 56 and
0x5fc0c8 from 68 to 44, each reasoned as the body length with the remainder belonging to a following function. Reading the
extent history showed that three of the four had been deliberately widened on 2026-10-25 by a reviewed boundary pass whose
stated invariant is that no text byte stays unowned: it folds a residual gap into the preceding entry because capstone
decodes the gap continuously with no new prologue, and it admits a gap as its own entry only when the gap starts a new
boundary. Under that invariant an over-long extent is the lesser defect, because the bytes are real code that would
otherwise belong to no row. All four are restored to their reviewed sizes, 4, 29, 73 and 68, through
`rebrew binary repair-extents` with the reason recorded in the history of each row. The general lesson is worth stating
because it will recur: a row whose object is shorter than its extent is not automatically an over-long extent, and shrinking
one must first re-derive the boundary, not just measure where the compiler stopped emitting bytes.

## 2026-11-03 — alignment fill is trimmed, continuation code is not

`0x507910` now measures RELOC at 213 of 213 with the object exactly at the extent and 18 relocations, after its extent was
settled at 213 against an inventoried 224. The row is the case that clarifies the boundary rule, because two policies met
here and one of them wins on the evidence. The body ends with `ret` at 0x507985, followed by a 16-entry jump table at
0x507988 and a 29-byte case-index table ending at 0x5079E5; every case target and table value already matched the source.
The eleven bytes from 0x5079E5 to the 16-aligned next row at 0x5079F0 are `0x90` fill, and the byte-identical GOLD twin at
0x5048E0 is already recorded at 213. C cannot emit table-trailing NOPs: eleven `__asm nop` statements after the switch were
tried and produced a 225-byte object with the match falling to 185, because the NOPs land before the compiler's own tables and
overwrite the return. So the eleven bytes are alignment, not code, and the extent is 213.
This refines the lesson recorded earlier for four other rows rather than contradicting it. A residual run that capstone
decodes continuously as code, with no new prologue, is a continuation of the same function and is kept inside the extent even
when the source stops short of it, which is why 0x5efd86, 0x65a20a, 0x64d1df and 0x5fc0c8 were restored to their reviewed
sizes. A run of `0x90` or `0xCC` after the last real content, filling to the next row's alignment, is padding and is trimmed,
which is why 0x51af00, 0x535bd0, 0x4f4830 and now 0x507910 are recorded at their content length. The distinguishing question
is not whether the object is short of the extent but whether the bytes are instruction-bearing code or fill.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 two: the home follows the live range, so deferral cannot free it

The probe proposed for `0x4DCF50` was run and came back negative, which settles the row's blocker rather than merely restating it.
The native first load of the p38 pointer is at 0x4dd0f2 through `mov ebx,eax`, after every head store, while this build assigns
it at source line 177, also after the head, so moving the assignment to match is a no-op. Deferring it to its first use at
line 208, or to after the p48 guard, was tested anyway along with deferring p34, p3c, p40 and p44. Nine variants, and the slot
is freed in none of them: with native's leading initialisers the frame stays at 0x764 and the first divergence sits at offset
zero on the frame byte, with 316 to 323 gap windows against the baseline 365, and on the baseline head the object shrinks to
8795 with 380 to 382 windows. The frame fix never appears, so the window count never drops sharply.
The evidence explains why. The pointer is not address-taken: there is no address-of in the source and no load-effective-address
of its slot in the object. It is stack-homed because its value stays live across regions where the allocator reuses ebx: the
baseline object stores it once at 0x197 with `mov [esp+0x18],ebx`, reuses ebx as a counter at 0x4fa, 0x54d, 0xab0, 0x148d,
0x193c and 0x1c6d, and reloads the value at 0x16b9 and 0x1c8a, while the reference pins p38 in ebx at 0x4dd0f2 and never
rewrites ebx. The value is really read at source lines 813 to 820, so the long live range is genuine rather than an artifact of
where the declaration sits, and deferring the first load moves the home without removing it, as the E2 variant shows when it
lands at 0x24 instead of 0x18. Freeing the slot therefore needs the loop region to stop reusing ebx, which is register
allocation shape and not source-level load placement. The row's blocker is rewritten with this and with the explicit list of
probes not to repeat. The source is restored byte-identically and nothing was kept.

`0x43C640` keeps 432 of 5512 with object 5512 against 5419 and 32 relocations, and no window closed, but the pass clears two

The file src/Develop/DieGildeAddOn/game/GOLDTL.fcn_004f4830.c holds three anchored definitions, and the function 0x4f4830 had
no anchor, so file-level commands resolved to the next definition: `rebrew diff` on the file reported a target size of 146
because the resolver takes the first address-anchored definition in source order and never errors on the ambiguity. The
listing proves the anchor: the inventory records 0x4f4830 with size 43 and an extent history of 48 to 43 from a reviewed
linker-fill tail on 2026-10-29, disassembly ends with `ret` at 0x4f485a followed by five NOP bytes and the next function at
0x4f4860, and the anchor was inserted directly above the declaration with only comments between it and the definition. All
three rows in the file were re-tested by explicit VA and are unchanged: 0x4f4830 at RELOC 43 of 43 with one validated
relocation, 0x4f48e0 at RELOC 146 of 146 with seven validated, and 0x4f5dd0 at RELOC 70 of 70 with two unresolved and one
validated. The GOLD twins of those rows are unaffected, and the GOLD side still resolves to 0x4f27d0 because GOLD.0x4f2720
has no GOLD anchor; that is recorded, not changed.
The stale coverage snapshot db/coverage-Europa1400Gold_TL.exe.toml records size 48 for this row against the reviewed 43. It is
wholesale-generated, dated 2026-10-27, predates the 2026-10-29 extent repair, and has one writer, the coverage export
command; a scratch re-export writes 43 with both tool sizes agreeing and src-relative paths in place of the stale basenames.
It was not edited, because regenerating is the repair.
One mistake is recorded rather than hidden. While checking whether the GOLD twin needed the same anchor, a test was run as
`rebrew test <file> --va 0x004f2720 --force-status` against the GoldTL target. That VA is a GOLD address and the GoldTL binary
holds different bytes there, so the run created a metadata row for a function the target does not have, with status STUB, and
reported a CONFLICT at offset 24 against native junk. The anchor added for GOLD was removed. The bogus row cannot be deleted
through the locked writer, because the only removal path is the orphan prune and it acts on all 1340 orphans in every store at
once, most of which are legitimate identity-only data rows whose definitions live in generated stubs outside src. The gap is
logged in the upstream checkout's docs/IDEAS-GUILD.md with a request for store, module and VA filters on the prune. Until that
lands, the row stays visible in the store and the next person should not test a GOLD VA against a GoldTL file.

figures do not reproduce from the source as described and the exact shape used for that measurement is unknown. The finding is
