## 2026-11-03 — a labelled codegen device worth two hundred and sixty bytes, and two operand fixes

`0x533090` moves from 141 to 408 matched bytes with the object at 1795 against the 1798 extent. Two operand repairs came first: the end test of a do loop was unsigned where the
reference uses a signed jump, and one call site exists twice in the reference with its argument setup duplicated per path where the source had one call through a temporary, so
the call is written once in each branch and the temporary assignments, dead past the call, are gone.
The large gain is a codegen device and is labelled as one in the source: the reference keeps a pointer that is only ever zero in a frame slot and reloads it, and keeps the
constant zero in a register this build assigns differently, which propagates into six shorter instruction forms and a different epilogue. Declaring that pointer volatile forces
a memory home and moves the row from 148 to 408 with the object inside its extent, semantics unchanged because the pointer is only compared and reloaded. The project already
carries this pattern for a field home in another row, and the device is commented in place rather than left as a bare qualifier.
Two candidate shapes were rejected: an integer-typed loop pointer and a conditional-expression argument both compiled identically, and a shared-tail restructure with a new
temporary measured worse. What remains is a register colour for the constant zero and three bytes of length, with the reference also null-checking a record pointer in a tail
shared by two cases where this build's merged condition drops the check.

## 2026-11-03 — the device lever does not generalise blindly: two rows measured against it

The labelled codegen device that moved one row from 148 to 408 was tried on two more rows this round and refused on both, with numbers rather than impressions. On the row
whose difference is one instruction of scheduling around a count load, a volatile output pointer cost sixty-seven matched bytes and a volatile argument cost eighty-four, both
because the qualifier removed the register reuse the reference depends on. On the row whose difference is which register receives each of three loaded globals, reordering the
assignment statements produced the identical object, confirming again that statement order at that level is not a lever.
The conclusion recorded for scheduling is that the device is a per-row diagnostic, not a default: it pays when the reference demonstrably keeps a value in a frame slot that this
build folds away, and it costs when the reference keeps the value in a register. The evidence to check first is whether the reference loads the value from memory more than once;
if it does, the device is the right shape, and if it does not, the device cannot help.

## 2026-11-03 — a ten-byte block where every memory home also moves the frame base

`0x4C6E20` stays at 113 of 123 after five device shapes were measured and refused. The block itself is an instruction-order swap with an identical instruction set: the reference
hoists the inlined copy count ahead of the two source-register moves, and this build places it after them. Every shape that gave the count a memory home also moved the frame
base by four bytes, which alone prevents a match at this row, and the shapes that left the count in a register produced byte-identical objects. Concretely: a volatile count
cost eighty-nine matched bytes and moved the frame base, a volatile destination cost sixty-two and spilled the pointer, a volatile source cost fifty-seven and reloaded it, a
separate accumulator compiled identically, and a volatile remaining count cost sixty-four and turned the counter into a memory increment.
The row is restored byte-identically and the recorded conclusion is that a memory home cannot be the lever where the frame base itself is part of the evidence.

## 2026-11-03 — a register swap that is allocator ordering, proved by six refusals

`0x50E170` stays at 100 of 121 with its object at the extent, after six shapes failed to change which register receives the call result and which receives the loop index. The
reference colours the result to one callee-saved register and the index to another; this build reverses them for every shape tried.
The measurements separate the two possible causes. Volatile homes move the frame, grow the body by ten to twenty-six bytes and lose forty-eight to ninety-six matched bytes, and
two of the three volatile shapes also change the save order away from the reference. A separate accumulator and single-element arrays of either value compile to objects that are
byte-identical to the baseline, because the compiler folds the extra name into the same scalar allocation. So the value's home is not the question at all: the allocator's
register assignment order is, and no source shape reaches it.
The row is restored and re-measured at its baseline. Together with the copy row, this closes the device lever's boundary: it pays when the reference reloads a value from memory
and the frame can absorb the home, and it cannot help a swap that exists only in the allocator's ordering.

`0x599350` stays at 728 of 1955 after seven device shapes, and the register evidence now isolates the swap to one pair. Forcing the flag to memory left the loop counter in

Unified layout: pad0 at 0, left at 4, top at 8, width at 0xc, height at 0x10, pad14 to 0x28, children at 0x28, count at 0x2c, pad30 to 0x38, surf at 0x38, pad3c to 0x27c, slot at 0x27c, pad280 to 0x290, active at 0x290, pad294 to 0x3a0, tex at 0x3a0, alpha at 0x3a4, tail to 0x3cc. - 2026-11-06: Literal-pool finding (`.scratch/consolidation-2026-11-05/slot-2/infer/B-literal-pools.md`). The literal-pool method reproduced msx.c and net.c exactly and consecutively in both binaries (msx literals immediately precede net literals; msx.c path literal is last in the msx block, net.c path literal sits inside the net block). The method did not reproduce main.c, aemter.c or d2_windows.c as single units: main.c members 0x538d00 and 0x544c50 are about 0xbf50 apart in `.text` with 147 other literals' referencers between them, aemter members span a 624-literal gap, and d2_windows members are spread over 32 literal slots. Main.c, aemter.c and d2_windows.c are therefore explicitly marked as inferred and contradicted by pool evidence; their merged placement is not a native TU claim.

- 2026-11-09: The server gate's d3dx8 screening reported 3,618 GoldTL findings (rebrew 6.20.0 and 6.24.0) against the 28 recorded earlier; the cause was an upstream bug, not the tree. Evidence: finding `0x00503e80` (game row `gm_FindNextFilteredEntity`, `spiel.c`, 341 bytes) was reported as `CD3DXTechnique::Initialize`, but `rebrew binary asm show 0x503e80` shows game code (`mov eax,[0x90e094]`, `cmp [0x773d88],0x100`) where the library body opens with a call to `__EH_prolog`; all 3,618 rows are FUNCTION rows, none LIBRARY. In `src/rebrew/lib_match.py`, commit `e438e776` (2026-11-05, a performance rewrite) skipped the byte comparison in `match_bytes` and `match_leading_body` whenever every relocation offset lay inside the compared window, so any same-size body with at least half fixed bytes matched any library symbol. Fixed in the upstream checkout as commit `b98b4dd1` (local, not pushed): one helper compares bytes and tolerates a mismatch only at a relocation offset, with a regression test that fails on the old code (`tests/test_lib_match.py`, both functions, plus the masked-byte case); the upstream suite passes (14,685 passed, 56 skipped). With the fixed source on `PYTHONPATH`, `rebrew library match --lib references/dxsdk8/lib/d3dx8.lib --target Europa1400Gold_TL.exe` returns 28 findings (`.scratch/d3dx8-match-fixed.json`), the count the project docs already carried. The project still pins released 6.24.0, so the gate prints 3,618 until a release contains the fix. Decision owner: user.
